limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

findings.text: 为维护多个DSH扩展的本机用户集中版本/兼容检查和逐项更新；验收正确profile、加载版本与核心功能。见[Q01](#research-q01)。
共享face选择官方RPC或loopback网关；profile线索→CLI/native writer→版本/组合核对→条件化重启计划，已知启动修复另有写入例外。见[Q02](#research-q02)。
独立子包manifest/bundle、GUI mount/详情/工具条与face真实RPC/HTTP、profile身份、兼容声明/更新查询、CLI/native主安装更新移除、配置enablement、启动修复与关键补偿/超时、重启计划/helper、共享围栏/遥测。未全审官方writer/CLI解析/所有包scripts与供应链、完整HMR/OS进程树、全部DOM和迁移布局，不执行目标。
包/registry/磁盘/重启、维护适配和异常恢复人工未知，串行批次有资源安排机制但不证明净节时/费用下降；表见[Q04](#research-q04)。

熟悉profile且能安排重启回归的用户，可在加载前外部备份的独立可弃置home和普通CLI测试profile，单项试用一个可信非关键direct npm包，确保没有其他writer。发现错profile、版本漂移、超时或恢复状态不明就停止后续任务并人工核磁盘/实例/功能，不把错误当未执行，也不以done/重启日志代替生效。精确版本审批、不可中断生产、桌面native替换或legacy迁移先观察，保留官方固定spec和人工回归办法。见[Q04](#research-q04)。
入口集中、版本/局部组合检查及条件重启有源码；查询覆盖、预览绑定、完整恢复与真实加载/业务成功未证。效果表见[Q04](#research-q04)。
可借鉴通道适配、profile一致性、排队任务串行、精确更新读回与owner-aware局部恢复；启动修复/外部writer、回滚异常和加载验证不被这些保护自动覆盖。见[Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)。
把多通道、兼容声明判定、逐项维护、实际版本回读和重启交接接入官方GUI；新增owner保护与有条件补偿真实存在。见[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q02](#research-q02)。
预览版本未绑定新latest，启动修复不入队，回滚/超时/查询完整性和运行加载都有条件；done、回滚日志和helper started不等功能恢复。见[Q03](#research-q03)。
先验证expectedVersion绑定、所有写入含启动修复入队及跨重启实际加载/功能回执；小补丁/人工清单够用就否定独立插件。见[Q05](#research-q05)。
需兼容宿主、正确profile/本机权限与对应官方writer、registry和可恢复旧来源；Node随宿主，本子包未单列engine。表见[Q04](#research-q04)。

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)成熟包/宿主之上GUI整合novelty9，未到新方法18；[Q02](#research-q02)profile/通道、owner保护和版本回读形成明确局部机制15，超零散接线8，但[Q03](#research-q03)未达跨实例/重启正确性23；条件化恢复思路可迁移10，协议/写入依赖未到普适15；[Q04](#research-q04)集中入口简化8，仍要备份/重启人工回归，未到11。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)主要集成既有维护入口workflow9，未改组织分工到18；[Q02](#research-q02)版本/组合回读是交付小幅8，仍不是功能验收新单元15；[Q04](#research-q04)GUI让既有本机DSH管理人群可达reach5，未证新群体10；[Q01](#research-q01)、[Q02](#research-q02)同实例串行批次/首错停止和集中重启安排改变维护资源组织，经济小幅4，仍逐包官方写入且恢复责任未变，未到8；净TCO/节时另记未知，非实测收益。

recommendation.reason: 熟悉DSH profile且能安排重启回归的用户，可在加载前外部备份的独立可弃置home和普通CLI测试profile，单项更新一个可信非关键direct npm扩展并保持没有其他writer。它把版本/兼容、真实依赖回读和重启交接集中到官方GUI，但预览未绑定新latest、启动修复未入队、部分回滚与加载未闭环，仍要核真实目标和新实例功能。错profile/版本漂移、错误/超时或恢复不明时停止后续任务且不重复提交，按实际状态用固定旧来源/备份和官方CLI恢复，生产批量、native替换及legacy迁移先观察。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)多扩展维护的profile/版本/重启交付具体，超泛管理入口15；频率和持续需求未测，未到30。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)实际通道/版本/owner检查超薄GUI6，但[Q03](#research-q03)目标绑定、修复竞态与恢复仍需人工，未到19。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)、[Q03](#research-q03)真实caller/写入/返回、native与CLI失败反证直接核，超README片段6；未安装/重启/并发或故障实验，未到19。

cost.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04)独立home、可信单包/外部备份可控小样支持超0；[Q03](#research-q03)加载自写、真实包与重启、异常/回滚恢复负担显著，未知工时/可恢复来源使其未到10。

publication.summaries.text: DSH插件管理扩展，在官方Plugins页面检查来源版本、逐项更新第三方包并安排重启，按宿主提供官方通道或本机网关。

items.界面: 官方Plugins详情更新区与列表第三方批量工具条
items.Host 路由: loopback网关的版本/安装更新移除、配置启停和重启计划
items.后台: 内存作业队列/轮询及启动后条件化profile行名修复

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 用途 | 条件与边界 |
|---|---|---|
| 版本/兼容检查 | 对照registry版本和DSH声明 | 查询失败可遗漏；不保证只升更高/每包已核 |
| 单项/批量更新 | 逐项官方writer维护 | 首错停后项；非整批事务、预览版本未绑定 |
| 配置启停/整理 | entry ID override、条件修复行名 | 当前加载另核；加载就可能写，修复未入队 |
| 状态/重启 | job与条件化重启交接 | 内存记录、请求/日志不等实例功能ready |

      "path": "packages/dsh-plugin-manager/README.md",
      "content": "# dsh-plugin-manager · Client Plugin Manager & Lifecycle Control UI for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)\n\nEnglish | [中文](README.zh.md)\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager?style=flat-square\" alt=\"Version\">\n   \n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%3E%3D0.2.1--rc.3-4c6ef5?style=flat-square&labelColor=454a54\" alt=\"DSH\">\n   \n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue?style=flat-square\" alt=\"License\">\n</p>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <strong>Client Plugin Manager & Lifecycle Control UI for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)</strong><br>\n  <em>Installed Plugin Version Checks · One-Click Batch Updates · Runtime Compatibility Gate · Safety Rollback · Dual Channels</em>\n</p>\n\nAn update and lifecycle manager for DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI and official desktop client: adds real-time registry version comparisons with DSH runtime compatibility checks directly into the official Plugins page, providing list-level batch updates, safe rollback mechanisms, and restart-to-apply workflows.\n\n## What it does\n\n- Contributes a check-for-updates block into the official Plugins page (the `plugins.detail.section` seat that page declares), rendered on an installed bundle's page and nowhere else. There is no tab of its own in the Plugins settings section.\n- Adds a list-level toolbar beside that page's **Installed** heading. The heading is the page's own chrome and the page declares no seat beside it (its extension points are `plugins.detail.*`, `plugins.item`, `plugins.bundle.config`, `plugins.row.config` and `plugins.bundle.activation`), so the toolbar is inserted into that element and kept in place through the family's shared body-mutation hub. One click checks every installed plugin; the panel lists the third-party rows that have a newer release, with the declared DSH minimum for any row this runtime is too old for; **Update all** applies the eligible rows one at a time with per-row progress and stops at the first failure, leaving the rest listed; **Restart now** then makes the update effective (see the restart note under Known limitations). Official `@deepseek-ai/` packages are never updated in bulk — their version belongs to the DSH installation.\n- Dual-channel transport: on runtimes with the official installer services (DSHCode and the 1.0.4 checkout web), every operation rides the official `/plugin-installer` and `/plugin-control` loopback RPC channels; on the npm-published web runtime those channels do not exist, so the package's host half mounts a loopback-fenced HTTP gateway that spawns the official `dsh plugin` CLI for installs/removals (the single writer) and writes `disabled` override rows for enablement. An application-owned profile (a packaged Desktop launch) takes the third writer for installs, updates and removals: the official in-process plugin manager the host mounts, because the CLI refuses to write that profile at all.\n- Detects the legacy aggregate `@linxin666/dsh-web-ui-all` and converts its update action into a transactional migration to `@linxin666/dsh-web-all`; the gateway removes the legacy package, installs the current package at an exact version, restores the legacy layer position, and verifies `--dump-config` before reporting success.\n- Verifies DSH runtime compatibility before npm updates (issue #754): update checks read the declared minimum DSH version from the latest manifest (`dsh.engines.dsh` with a top-level `engines.dsh` fallback), evaluate it as a node-semver range with the call the official boot gate makes — `semver.satisfies(host, range, { includePrerelease: true })` — so `||` alternatives, `^` and `~`, whitespace-separated comparators and x-ranges decide here exactly as they decide at boot, and show the requirement beside the update action. A requirement the running DSH does not satisfy disables the action and says to upgrade DSH. A requirement the host could not verify — an unreadable running version, or a declaration that is not a range node-semver parses — is a different verdict with its own copy: it names no cause and never sends the user to upgrade a DSH that was never compared. Neither verdict lets the update run, and the host update route answers 412 before starting any CLI job in both cases.\n- Protects the next boot on the npm runtime: after each install the gateway verifies the dependency actually landed, rejects duplicate entry-id claims and insert rows naming unresolvable packages, and composes the profile with the CLI's `--dump-config` preflight; a conflicting or failing install is rolled back through the official remove path and the existing plugins are never touched.\n\n## Install\n\n### From npm (recommended)\n\n```sh\ndsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager\n```\n\n### From the repository (development)\n\n```sh\ngit clone https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web.git\ncd dsh-web\npnpm install && pnpm -r build\ndsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)/packages/dsh-plugin-manager\n```\n\nRestart `dsh web`; the update block appears on a bundle's page inside the official Plugins panel.\n\n## Config\n\nThe package carries no configuration namespace. Update writes apply at the next restart.\n\n## Cordis service\n\nThe browser half provides the shared dual-channel face as the cordis service `pluginManager`, so sibling client plugins can drive and observe plugin management without re-implementing the channel detection. Consume it with `ctx.inject(['pluginManager'], cb)` and read `ctx.pluginManager`:\n\n- `isLoopback: boolean` — whether this browser has loopback authority to use the host routes.\n- `list(): Promise<InstalledPluginItem[]>` — read the installed snapshot.\n- `install(spec): Promise<InstalledPluginItem>` — install one plugin from an npm spec or git URL.\n- `uninstall(id): Promise<InstalledPluginItem[]>` — remove one plugin.\n- `status(): Promise<InstallProgressItem>` — read the current install/update progress.\n- `failures(): Promise<PluginFailuresSnapshot>` — read the recorded plugin boot-failure ring (plugin id, message, stack, install path); runtimes without a ring answer an empty snapshot.\n- `setEnabled(id, enabled): Promise<InstalledPluginItem>` — flip one plugin's next-start enablement through the active channel (official installer RPC or gateway patch `disabled` row); takes effect after the host restart.\n- `onChange(cb): () => void` — subscribe to successful mutations; fires after `install()`, `update()`, `uninstall()`, or `setEnabled()` resolves, and returns the unsubscribe function.\n\nThe contract source of truth is `src/core/service.ts` (`PluginManagerService`). The service is provided for the plugin's lifetime and disappears when the plugin is unloaded. The service and the update block share one face, so `onChange` subscribers observe the same mutations.\n\n## Known limitations\n\n- Loopback-only: on a LAN or remote browser the update block renders a local-only notice (the same boundary the official installer page enforces; the gateway refuses non-loopback requests with 403).\n- On the npm-published web runtime, gateway writes go through the official CLI. The gateway resolves `dsh` from the host process PATH first, then from `node_modules/.bin` project roots above the running host entry, then from the running host package's own `lib/bin.js`, and finally from the packaged Desktop install's own CLI launcher under the Electron resource directory (`runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd` on Windows, `runtime/cli/bin/dsh` elsewhere) — the last one covers a packaged Desktop, where the host runs from inside `app.asar`, the private host package ships no `lib/bin.js`, every `.bin` shim directory is stripped from the installer, and the launcher puts only the bundled `node` on the host's PATH. A Node-script CLI (an npm or homebrew shim, a `.bin` symlink, a `lib/bin.js`) runs under an interpreter resolved without PATH: the `node` installed beside the CLI when the installation ships one, otherwise the host's own interpreter. The CLI's own directory goes first on the child PATH, so the `dsh plugin` run finds the pnpm installed beside it. If no source contains the CLI, CLI-backed writes remain unavailable — an application-owned profile writes through the official in-process manager and needs no binary, so its install, update and removal routes never demand one. CLI output is decoded as bytes in one pass, so a Windows console's code page (CP936/GBK) renders as readable text instead of replacement characters. Installs of git sources can take minutes and run as background jobs. Gateway updates apply only to npm registry sources, resolve the latest version on the host, and succeed only after the same installed package reports that exact version.\n- An application-owned profile (the packaged Desktop client) runs installs, updates and removals through the official in-process plugin manager the host mounts, the same writer that profile's official Plugins page drives: the CLI refuses `--profile desktop` outright, and the launcher hands that manager its bundled package-manager invocation. The job, its status polling and its verification are identical to the CLI path — an install must add a dependency the profile did not carry, a removal must drop one, and an update must still report the version the route resolved — while the CLI-specific guards (duplicate-mount stripping, insert-row and boot preflight) stay with the CLI writer, because there the official manager validates and applies the bundle itself. The manager's own verdict is read before the profile is: it resolves a refused run with `application: 'failed'` instead of rejecting, so the job reports that run's real reason (the pnpm diagnostic, or the packages an incompatible-version refusal names) rather than a no-op after an unchanged profile. Since 0.2.1-rc.2 that manager also refuses to install a dependency the profile already carries while the host mounts `hmr` — every profile host — so an update there runs as its two phases instead: remove the installed bundle, then install the target spec through the same manager, and a second phase that fails reinstalls the spec the profile carried before the run, so a failed update leaves a working plugin rather than an empty slot. The single call stays first, so an upstream in-place update would need no change here. Every other runtime keeps the CLI as the single writer of installs, updates and removals.\n- Compatibility gating applies only when the target manifest declares a minimum DSH version; packages without `dsh.engines.dsh` update unchecked, and official-installer runtimes (DSHCode and the checkout web) are not gated here because their updates go through the official installer. The running DSH version is read from the installation's own `@deepseek-ai/dsh` manifest, which the launcher publishes as the profile's install anchor — no subprocess, no PATH, and therefore an answer on a packaged Desktop host — with `dsh --version` kept as the fallback for a runtime that publishes no anchor. A requirement the host cannot verify at all is reported as unverified rather than as a version below the minimum: both hold the update back, but only the second sends the user to upgrade DSH.\n- Enablement on the npm runtime reports the effective next-start value: a profile override row wins where present, otherwise the installed bundle's own `disabled` rows decide (the aggregate's inactive-by-default families), and rows no layer mentions are enabled. Enabling a row the bundle disables writes an explicit `disabled: false` override, because deleting the user row would only restore the bundle default; the runtime's loader honors these rows at the next start, but this path is less exercised than the official desktop writer's.\n- Restart is explicit, user-clicked and three-mode. The route is method-aware: `GET /api/plugin-manager/restart` reads the plan (no side effects, so a prefetch or a typed URL can never stop a host) and `POST` carries it out; every other method is refused with 405. The toolbar reads the plan first, so the confirmation names the same consequence the host will produce. On a terminal launch (`dsh web`) the host starts a detached helper that waits for the outgoing process to exit and then re-executes the same command line, so the port is free before the replacement binds it, and the replacement's output goes to `$DSH_HOME/logs/plugin-manager-restart.log`. Under the packaged Desktop app the plugin cannot relaunch anything — Electron owns the process tree, a detached respawn would fight the shell for the same port, and the official shell answers a host exit with `fail(\"dsh desktop host stopped\")` and an error page, because it exposes no way to ask the shell to restart — so the host exits there only when the shell exports `DSH_SHELL_RESTARTS_HOST=1`, its own declaration that an exiting host is brought back. Without that guarantee the restart panel states that this process cannot restart itself, names the manual way out (quit DeepSeek Harness and open it again), and offers no confirmation button: that path would not restart anything. A launch with no terminal (a supervisor, an editor task) is left running and the toolbar says to restart manually. Without a restart, updated plugin code is loaded at the next start.\n- On the npm runtime, duplicate insert-id claims are detected after install and the new plugin is rolled back automatically (a shared id can never be `disabled` away: the loader's duplicate check has no disabled exemption).\n- The npm runtime's boot preflight (`--dump-config`) catches composition failures, and the static insert check catches insert rows naming packages that resolve nowhere; runtime import/apply failures still surface only at the next real start.\n- Duplicate-mount safeguard (gateway mode): the official CLI's bundle reconciliation re-adds every bundle-declaring dependency to `dsh.profile.bundles` after any install/remove — including packages the composition already mounts through a patch row (a bundle that mounts an external plugin by row), which would double-mount and fail the next boot (`duplicate prefix route`). After every successful CLI mutation the gateway strips exactly the newly added, already-row-mounted bundles entries back out (the manifest write goes through backup + tmp + atomic rename), reports one notice per stripped entry on the job result, and leaves normal installs' bundles entries — and every entry the user had before — untouched.\n- The wire shapes mirror the official installer protocol; on drift the tolerant parsers degrade to error rows rather than misbehaving.\n\n## Security model\n\n- Trust boundary is the loopback fence: every gateway route requires a loopback socket address, a loopback Host header, and a non-cross-site origin (socket + Host + Origin + `sec-fetch-site`), the same authority the official installer channels enforce. There is no browser-reachable path from a remote origin; rejected requests receive HTTP 403 with `{ ok: false, error: \"forbidden: loopback-only\" }`.\n- Mutation routes (install / update / remove / set-enabled / restart) carry no token: the loopback authority *is* the local user, matching the official channels. The restart route is the one route whose effect is process-level: it never invents a command line (it re-executes this process's own `execPath` + argv, dropping inspector flags), it refuses to relaunch anything it cannot identify as a terminal launch, and under the packaged Desktop app it stops this process only when the shell declares `DSH_SHELL_RESTARTS_HOST=1`. Any local process can therefore drive plugin installs and removals, and npm installs run package install scripts — treat the gateway as local code execution by design and never expose it beyond loopback.\n- Install specs and package ids are rejected when they contain command-shell expansion characters or control characters. On Windows, npm shims are resolved to `node.exe` plus the package `bin.js`; packaged Desktop shims have no adjacent npm layout, so they run through `cmd.exe /d /s /c` with a pre-quoted, verbatim argument envelope. That command processor is addressed by absolute path (`ComSpec`, otherwise `%SystemRoot%\\System32\\cmd.exe`) instead of by bare name, so a host whose PATH omits the system directories still runs the shim; a spawn that still fails settles as a failed job carrying the reason instead of taking the dsh host process down. Desktop profile discovery reads the packaged launcher's profile environment value or persisted profile selection, and application-owned profile installs, updates and removals run in the host half through the mounted official `pluginManager` service — the same writer that profile's official Plugins page drives through its own RPC face — under the same loopback fence and user click.\n- Mutations are serialized through one queue, so concurrent jobs never interleave their before/after profile captures. An install is only `done` when the new dependency actually landed in the profile (and a removal only when it is gone); a success exit code alone is never trusted.\n- Enablement re-reads the current profile manifest under that mutation queue and rejects stale or unknown package ids with `404` before writing, so a panel row left behind by an uninstall cannot create an orphan `disabled` override.\n- Conflict handling is owner-aware: a duplicate entry id or an insert row naming an unresolvable package rolls the *new* package back through the official remove path. The gateway never writes `disabled` rows for a shared id (such rows cannot stop the loader's duplicate check and would flag the existing owner).\n- The boot preflight (`--dump-config`) composes patch layers without importing entries: it catches composition failures, not import-time failures, which still surface at the first real boot.\n- The boot profile resolves from `--profile`, then the launched profile the Host publishes on `profileContext`, then the profile directory the packaged launcher carries in its own argv (Electron strips exec switches, so the desktop host sees its profile directory positionally), then `DSH_PROFILE`, then the `web` subcommand, then the packaged app's persisted selection. The published profile outranks the variable because the packaged Desktop client exports neither and a global `DSH_PROFILE` workaround can name a profile the running Host never reads.\n- The launched profile the Host publishes is foreign input: its name is traversal-checked, its directory must be an absolute traversal-free path, and its patch path is accepted only when it is that profile's own `cordis.patch.yml` — the patch path is a write target. Patch writes go through a backup copy plus tmp-write + atomic rename (`cordis.patch.yml.bak-plugin-manager`).\n- The duplicate-mount safeguard writes only the profile manifest's `dsh.profile.bundles`, under the same backup + tmp-write + atomic-rename discipline as patch writes (`package.json.bak-plugin-manager`). It removes only entries the CLI just added that duplicate an existing patch-row mount, and a failed safeguard write fails the job visibly rather than silently leaving a boot-breaking state.\n\n## Telemetry\n\nThe browser half sends one anonymous install heartbeat per UTC day to dsh-market.com: a random localStorage id plus this package's name, nothing else. The server stores only a salted hash of that id, never IP addresses, and exposes aggregate counts only. 的 Linux `systemd-inhibit`），允许显示器正常关闭的同时阻止整机因闲置休眠，确保夜间无人值守巡检与流水线准时打卡。\n- **多 Agent 树状级联并发与原生 Agent Teams 团队编排**：复杂工程目标可自由拆解为多层树状子任务（支持 1~3 运行时与高效调度引擎）\n\n在新建会话输入框左侧通过专属老虎机拨杆切换，或在“设置 > Agent 预设”中选用。梁神模式（`dsh-liangshen`）是专为追求**极致推理效率、超低静态上下文开销与严苛工程执行纪律**而深度重构的杀手级预设与运行时插件。针对主流大模型在长程编程任务中容易出现的系统提示词冗长膨胀、工具 Schema 挤占上下文、思维链无效空转（如“流水账推理”）以及多轮遗忘退化等痛点，梁神模式通过原生极简提示词、程序化代码工具调用（PTC）、MCP 温和分页与关键事实局部就近投射，提供纯粹而强悍的编程作战体验：\n\n- **极简 Persona 与严苛行动导向纪律（Zero Prompt Waste）**：彻底剥离官方 Standard 预设中冗长繁琐的系统级条文，将提示词极致收敛为单行 Persona 与经过实战千锤百炼的高效工程纪律。内置反思熔断（同一假设推演不超过两轮，缺少事实立即闭合思考并调用原生工具探测，杜绝凭空揣测）、行动导向（思考过程仅用于决定下一步具体操作，严禁在思考中预演完整代码）、并发探索（单轮内并发派发多个独立检测或搜索工具）、YAGNI 与 PDCA 循环（单步验证单一假设，不写冗余注水注释）、以及有界收敛纪律（前置检查最多 2-3 轮即刻收敛，迅速转入实际作答或编辑）。大幅降低静态 Token 占用，让模型注意力百分之百倾注于业务与代码本身。\n- **程序化工具调用传输（PTC · Programmatic Tool Calling）**：彻底终结在每次请求中平铺上百个 JSON Schema 工具参数的低效模式。默认将网络线协议（wire）极致收拢为唯一的 `run_code`（运行 TypeScript 脚本），其余所有工具均通过自动生成的强类型 SDK 在独立的沙箱线程中以代码形式调用。无论系统注册了多少复杂工具，静态传输面始终保持极小体积；模型可原生利用 `Promise.all` 编写并发工具调用，并在程序内预先过滤、聚合、提取关键数据，只将精炼结论回传至对话上下文，从根本上解决大文本输出打爆 Token 的问题。对于习惯原生工具面的场景，亦可在插件设置中一键无缝切换为组装好的原生工具清单（Native）。\n- **MCP 工具温和分页与 LRU 动态激活（Gentle Tool Paging）**：针对海量 MCP 工具或第三方插件扩展，出厂默认启用温和分页（默认匹配 `mcp__*`）。外部工具在初始状态下仅以命名空间摘要形式登记在目录消息中，既不占 wire 协议也不进 SDK 声明；当大模型判定需要使用对应工具时，可自主调用 `tool_activate({ namespace })` 按需挂载。内置 LRU 策略（上限 3 个活跃命名空间），自动淘汰最久未用的命名空间，激活状态在会话压缩与恢复后完整重建，兼具海量工具接入能力与极致小巧的静态 Schema 面。\n- **关键事实登记簿与就近状态投射（Fact Register & Working Context）**：长程多轮对话中大模型极易遗忘早期的关键业务约束或踩过的坑。插件向模型提供专属 `fact_register` 工具，可将用户硬性约束、已确认的架构决策或失败路径登记为单行事实（每条不超过 160 字符，最多保留 12 条）。关键事实随 `[Working Context: ...]` 状态行在每一轮交互中就近投射至最新消息尾部的局部注意力窗口内，从物理机制上彻底解决长上下文“中间遗忘”与重复踩坑顽疾。\n- **原生调度者架构与敏捷访谈纪律（Dispatcher Identity & Triage）**：预设出厂深度集成调度者（Dispatcher）架构规范，赋能模型以团队指挥官身份统领工程任务。内置复杂度分诊机制（L0/L1 单点任务直接敏捷执行，L2 复杂任务严格遵循“澄清访谈 -> 架构规划 -> 并发子代理派发 -> 双层严格验收”标准流）；设定严格的提问预算控制（单轮最多 4 问、总计最多 3 轮、影响面排序、假设先行），杜绝无效拉扯；任务状态权威沉淀于 `todo_write`，杜绝浮躁的敷衍式交付。\n- **新建会话老虎机拨杆与炫酷中奖特效（Composer Slot Lever）**：在新建会话输入框工具行、模型选择器左侧，精心打造了一台复古老虎机拨杆控件。下拉拨杆（支持鼠标拖拽、单击或键盘快捷操作）即可一键为当前新建会话装配梁神模式，拉下命中即触发绚丽的中奖粒子特效（闪光、冲击环、火花粒子与专属彩蛋横幅）；上推即可平滑切回默认模式。拨杆自适应全局主题色彩，且在会话开始后自动隐藏，丝滑灵动，极具极客趣味。\n\n详细机制、评测数据与高级配置参数见 [dsh-liangshen README](packages/dsh-liangshen/README.zh.md)。\n\n### 移动端远程控制（Mobile Remote · 手机访问与跨设备触控优化）\n\n通过侧边栏底部的手机图标打开设备配对面板。使用手机扫码或复制链接配对后，手机浏览器将直接载入官方 Web |\n\n### 会话归档管理（Session Archive Manager · 全文检索与生命周期策略）\n\n会话归档管理（`dsh-session-archive`）是专为解决大量长短期会话堆积而设计的集中管理模块，随全家桶安装生效：\n\n- **集中检索与状态筛选**：统一呈现活跃会话、已归档会话、空白会话、子代理派生会话以及无工作区会话，支持按标题、工作区、状态及会话 ID **自动化生命周期策略**：提供两个默认关闭的自动化策略：根据最后活跃时间自动归档、根据归档时间自动清理超期数据，支持在启用前进行结果预览与单次手动执行。\n\n删除操作不可逆，所有管理路由严格限制本机回环访问。详细机制见 [dsh-session-archive README](packages/dsh-session-archive/README.zh.md)。\n\n### 暗黑沉浸风格预览](docs/screenshots/17-skin-blue-fantasy-dark.png)\n\n## 快速上手\n\n### 系统要求\n\n- 已安装 DeepSeek Harness 且 `dsh web` 可正常启动。\n- npm 安装方式无需额外环境；若从源码仓库构建，需要 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm 环境。\n\n### 三步上手（npm [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md)。\n\n### 安装排障\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>展开查看常见安装与构建排障方案</strong></summary>\n\n<br>\n\n> **pnpm 严格依赖隔离导致模块找不到**：pnpm 的 isolated 模式默认仅将聚合包放置在顶层，部分子包可能被嵌套收敛，导致 `dsh web` 启动时报错 `Cannot find package '@linxin666/dsh-...'`。若遇到此情况，可在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中添加配置 `nodeLinker: hoisted`（或 `public-hoist-pattern: ['@linxin666/*']`）后重新安装。\n\n> **构建脚本被拦截 (ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS)**：这三项审批必须在首次 add 之前就位。正确顺序是重置 profile（官方 `--from-default-profile web`）或换新 profile，把 `cloudflared`、`cpu-features`、`ssh2` 写进 `<profile>/pnpm-workspace.yaml` 的 `allowBuilds`，再执行 add。装失败后补审批重跑会 exit 0，但 `dsh.profile.bundles` 仍无该行：静默半挂载，重跑修不回来。已带审批的存量 profile 升级不受影响。\n\n> **pnpm 11 发布时间门禁问题**：在包版本发布后的短时间内，pnpm 11 的默认安全策略（`minimumReleaseAge`）可能会尝试回退拉取旧版本。建议在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中排除相关命名空间以确保获取最新版本：\n>\n> ```yaml\n> minimumReleaseAgeExclude:\n>   - '@linxin666/*'\n> ```\n\n</details>\n\n## 兼容性与运行环境\n\ndsh-web 针对主流操作系统、现代化浏览器及网络拓扑进行了深度工程调优与兼容性保障：\n\n| 维度 | 支持范围与技术规格 |\n| --- | --- |\n| 宿主运行环境 | DeepSeek Harness CLI (`dsh web`)、官方桌面客户端（DeepSeek Harness Desktop） |\n| 操作系统 | macOS (Apple Silicon M 系列 & Intel 芯片)、Windows 10/11 (含 WSL2)、Linux (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Arch, CentOS 等) |\n| 浏览器与设备 | 桌面浏览器 (Chrome, Edge, Safari, Firefox)；移动端现代浏览器 (iOS Safari, Android Chrome 等) |\n| 网络连接架构 | 本机环回访问 (127.0.0.1)、局域网多设备互联 (LAN)、公网隧道安全穿透 (Cloudflare Tunnel, Tailscale, FRP, Nginx 反向代理) |\n| 模型供应商覆盖 | DeepSeek 官方通道与满血模型、OpenAI (GPT-4o 等)、Anthropic Claude、Google Gemini、Kimi (Moonshot)、GLM (智谱)、MiniMax、Ollama 本地大模型、SiliconFlow 等 |\n| 运行时依赖 | npm 方式安装无特殊环境依赖；源码编译需 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm >= 9 |\n\n## 常见问题\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>安装重启后，侧边栏未显示插件入口？</strong></summary>\n\n请首先检查插件是否正确安装至 `web` profile（命令需包含 `--profile web`），并通过 `dsh --profile web --dump-config` 验证配置层是否已成功挂载。注意仅刷新网页无法加载新模块，必须彻底重启 `dsh web` 后端服务进程。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>定时任务为何未能按时触发执行？</strong></summary>\n\n任务调度完全由 `dsh web` 后端宿主进程驱动，无需保持前端浏览器页面打开。若宿主进程退出、系统关机或整机进入深度睡眠，错过的触发时间点将遵循跳过策略处理，不执行回填补跑；若任务到达触发点时上一轮仍在运行，会自动顺延至下一个周期。若需要允许息屏但防止主机自动睡眠，可开启任务看板自带的电源保护选项。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>手机端配对后为何没有收到流式推送？</strong></summary>\n\n流式推送走官方 WebSocket 通道，配对后经门控的 `/remote` 代理转发。隧道中断期间更新暂停，通道恢复后继续，无需重新配对；更新节奏的差异来自远程链路的广域网往返延迟。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>试穿主题皮肤不满意如何还原？</strong></summary>\n\n皮肤面板提供免落盘试穿功能：点击试穿即刻在当前界面生效预览，离开面板或关闭预览会自动恢复初始外观；只有显式点击“应用”按钮才会将主题配置写入磁盘，可放心预览各类主题。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>是否可以仅使用主题皮肤或某个单一插件？</strong></summary>\n\n完全支持。若仅需要视觉定制，直接安装 `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-skin-center` 即可；若仅需特定功能，参考“单独安装某个插件”章节直接安装对应 npm 包即可。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>已安装全家桶的前提下，能否额外独立安装某个子插件？</strong></summary>\n\n可以。聚合包内部的插件注册标识均统一带有 `web-ui-` 前缀（例如 `web-ui-usage`），与独立包的原生标识（如 `usage`）相互独立，不会产生 loader entry 重复冲突。宿主服务对同类插件会自动去重。通常情况下安装全家桶即可满足完整需求，无需重复安装单个子包。\n\n</details>\n\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>如何通过手机或平板远程访问 DeepSeek Harness？是否必须在同一 Wi-Fi 下？</strong></summary>\n\n手机远程访问基于配对令牌安全门控。若手机与运行 DSH 的电脑处于同一局域网（Wi-Fi），电脑端点击侧边栏手机图标弹出二维码，手机直接扫码即可打开完整的移动端交互界面。若需要公网跨网络访问（例如在户外使用移动蜂窝网络访问家中电脑），可搭配 Cloudflare Tunnel（例如 cloudflared）或 Tailscale 将 DSH 端口穿透至公网，手机打开公网链接配对访问即可，通信全程走鉴权通道，未配对请求将被严格拦截。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>关闭浏览器或电脑休眠后，DeepSeek 的定时任务还会继续运行吗？</strong></summary>\n\n任务调度完全由 `dsh web` 后端宿主进程驱动，关闭浏览器标签页不影响定时任务的触发与执行。但如果整机进入深度睡眠或关机，宿主进程将暂停运行，离线期间错过的触发点会遵循跳过策略处理。若希望保持无人值守后台自动化，可在任务看板设置中开启“电源保护”选项，该选项会阻止系统因空闲进入休眠（允许显示器正常熄灭），确保定时任务准时触发。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>如何查看和监控 DeepSeek 及其他模型 API 的 Token 消耗与账户余额？</strong></summary>\n\n安装使用统计插件后，在“设置 > 使用统计”面板中可查看按日汇总的输入、输出与缓存 Token 数量，支持按模型细分查看 30 天消费趋势。针对 DeepSeek 官方路由还提供峰谷分时计费估算；若配置了支持查询余额的供应商 API，插件可定时拉取当前账户剩余额度与重置周期。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>多个 AI 智能体（Agent）并发编码时，如何避免 Git 分支和代码冲突？</strong></summary>\n\n直接在单一 Git 工作区并发运行多个智能体容易导致代码互相覆盖。使用全家桶内置的 Git 图谱插件，可以在新建会话时自动或手动创建独立的 Git Worktree。每个智能体会话在各自专属的分支和物理目录中独立运行、提交修改，彻底隔绝主工作区文件，开发完成后可在图谱面板中清晰比对并合并分支。\n\n</details>\n\n## 已知限制\n\n- 任务看板由后端 Host 进程统一调度，关闭前端标签页不影响任务执行；但若宿主进程停止或操作系统关机睡眠，处于离线期间的触发点将直接跳过不补跑。可选的电源保护仅阻止系统闲置睡眠，无法阻止用户主动合盖、手动休眠或电源切断，技术细节见 [dsh-task-board README](packages/dsh-task-board/README.zh.md)。\n- SSH 凭据（密码与私钥口令）保存在本地 `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json` 文件中（文件权限为 0600）；在网络中断重连时可能重新发送非幂等命令，终端输出保持原样返回不执行脱敏，安全规范见 [dsh-ssh README](packages/dsh-ssh/README.zh.md)。\n- 移动端流式输出经隧道或固定域名中继转发，广域网往返延迟叠加在每次更新上；固定域名中继比裸快速隧道多一跳，两者都可用。\n- 从源码构建全仓需要 Node.js >= 22 与 pnpm 工具链，直接从 npm 安装不受此限制。\n\n## 社区\n\n欢迎加入社区交流群，与开发者及其他用户探讨使用技巧、反馈使用问题或提出新功能建议。\n\n扫描下方二维码加入“DSH Web 交流群”：\n\n<img src=\"docs/community-center.jpg\" alt=\"DeepSeek Harness       "path": "packages/dsh-plugin-manager/cordis.patch.yml",
      "content": "# bundle patch for the dsh-plugin-manager plugin: inserts its plugin row into the web\n# profile roster. Applied as a profile bundle layer (the `dsh.bundle.patch`\n# manifest field); install with\n# `dsh plugin --profile web add link:<repo>/packages/dsh-plugin-manager`.\n#\n# The row id lives in the loader's GLOBAL id space, one entry per id with\n# later-wins and no diagnostic. The official @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app bundle\n# already claims `ui-plugin-manager` for its own plugin page (the half that\n# registers the sidebar \"Plugins\" entry), so this package claims its own id\n# instead; sharing the official id dropped the official row silently and the\n# sidebar entry disappeared with the whole plugin management page.\n#\n# The row `name` must stay exactly the package name: the official\n# @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-modules mounts a package's browser half on the loader\n# row whose specifier resolves to that package's own manifest, so a subpath\n# name (the aggregate's `@linxin666/dsh-web-all/plugin-manager` shape) would\n# mount the host half only.\n- insert:\n    - id: ui-plugin-manager-update-check\n      name: '@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager'\n"
    },

      "path": "packages/dsh-plugin-manager/src/client/PluginListToolbar.tsx",
      "content": "/**\n * The list-level toolbar: check every installed third-party plugin for a newer\n * registry release, apply them in one run, then restart DSH to load them.\n *\n * It exists because the official Plugins page compares one package at a time\n * (its `plugins.detail.section` contributions render on a bundle's page), while\n * the answer a user wants when they open the page is \"is anything of mine out\n * of date, and can I just fix it\". It is mounted beside the page's \"Installed\"\n * heading (see plugin-toolbar-mount.tsx) because that heading is the page's own\n * chrome and the page declares no seat next to it.\n *\n * Policy lives in core/updates.ts (third-party only, compatibility-gated) and\n * the operations come from the injected face, so this component is pure\n * rendering plus the sequence of calls: nothing here touches the DOM beyond its\n * own subtree.\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager/client\n */\n\nimport { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react'\nimport type { PropsLocale } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots'\nimport type { PluginUpdateItem, PluginUpdateResult, RestartMode } from '../core/protocol.ts'\nimport { applicableUpdates, thirdPartyUpdates } from '../core/updates.ts'\nimport { displayMinimumVersion } from '../core/version.ts'\nimport { dshGateOf } from './PluginUpdatePatch.tsx'\nimport css from './plugin-manager.module.css'\n\n/** The operations the toolbar drives (the package's dual-channel face). */\nexport interface PluginListToolbarInjected {\n  /** Whether this browser has loopback authority to use the host routes. */\n  isLoopback: boolean\n  /** Compare every installed plugin against the version its source serves. */\n  checkUpdates: () => Promise<PluginUpdateItem[]>\n  /**\n   * Re-install one plugin from its recorded source. Resolves with what landed:\n   * the row at the new version, plus the bundles only a restart loads. A landed\n   * update that needs a restart keeps the batch running instead of failing it.\n   */\n  update: (id: string) => Promise<PluginUpdateResult>\n  /**\n   * Read how a restart would be carried out, without carrying it out: the\n   * confirmation must name the same consequence the host will produce (an\n   * in-place relaunch, the packaged Desktop shell's own recovery dialog, or a\n   * manual restart), and a plan read has no side effects.\n   */\n  restartPlan: () => Promise<RestartMode>\n  /** Restart the host so an applied update is loaded. */\n  restart: () => Promise<RestartMode>\n}\n\n/** Full component props. */\nexport type PluginListToolbarProps =\n  & PropsLocale<'settings.pluginManager'>\n  & PluginListToolbarInjected\n\n/** Error text for a caught request or lifecycle failure. */\nfunction messageOf(error: unknown): string {\n  if (error instanceof AggregateError) {\n    const details = error.errors.map(messageOf).join('; ')\n    return details === '' ? error.message : `${error.message}: ${details}`\n  }\n  return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)\n}\n\n/** What the toolbar is currently doing. */\ntype Phase = 'idle' | 'checking' | 'updating'\n\n/** Which flyout is open under the buttons. */\ntype Panel = 'none' | 'list' | 'restart'\n\n/**\n * The toolbar itself. All state is local: the page around it owns the plugin\n * list, and a restart tears this component down anyway.\n */\nexport function PluginListToolbar(props: PluginListToolbarProps) {\n  const { t, isLoopback, checkUpdates, update, restartPlan, restart } = props\n\n  const [phase, setPhase] = useState<Phase>('idle')\n  const [checked, setChecked] = useState(false)\n  /** Every third-party row the last check reported, including the applied ones. */\n  const [found, setFound] = useState(0)\n  const [rows, setRows] = useState<PluginUpdateItem[]>([])\n  const [applied, setApplied] = useState<string[]>([])\n  /**\n   * Updates this run applied whose new version the running host has not loaded,\n   * with the version that landed. They stay in `applied` — the update did go\n   * through — and are listed as needing a restart instead of leaving the panel\n   * claiming a plain success.\n   */\n  const [restartRequired, setRestartRequired] = useState<{ id: string; version: string }[]>([])\n  const [cursor, setCursor] = useState<{ name: string; index: number; total: number } | undefined>(undefined)\n  const [error, setError] = useState<string | undefined>(undefined)\n  const [panel, setPanel] = useState<Panel>('none')\n  /** How the host says it would restart, read before the confirmation is shown. */\n  const [plan, setPlan] = useState<RestartMode | undefined>(undefined)\n  const [restartMode, setRestartMode] = useState<RestartMode | undefined>(undefined)\n  /** Synchronous in-flight mirror of the phase: a click and a keypress can land in one frame. */\n  const busyRef = useRef(false)\n\n  const pending = applicableUpdates(rows)\n\n  /** Close the flyout on Escape, the shell's own dismissal gesture. */\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (panel === 'none') return\n    const onKey = (event: KeyboardEvent): void => {\n      if (event.key === 'Escape') setPanel('none')\n    }\n    window.addEventListener('keydown', onKey)\n    return () => { window.removeEventListener('keydown', onKey) }\n  }, [panel])\n\n  const onCheck = (): void => {\n    if (busyRef.current) return\n    busyRef.current = true\n    setPhase('checking')\n    setError(undefined)\n    setRestartMode(undefined)\n    void checkUpdates().then(items => {\n      const thirdParty = thirdPartyUpdates(items)\n      setRows(thirdParty)\n      setFound(thirdParty.length)\n      setApplied([])\n      setRestartRequired([])\n      setChecked(true)\n      setPanel('list')\n    }).catch(reason => {\n      setError(t('failed', { reason: messageOf(reason) }))\n      setPanel('list')\n    }).finally(() => {\n      busyRef.current = false\n      setPhase('idle')\n    })\n  }\n\n  const onUpdateAll = (): void => {\n    if (busyRef.current) return\n    const queue = applicableUpdates(rows)\n    if (queue.length === 0) return\n    busyRef.current = true\n    setPhase('updating')\n    setError(undefined)\n    void (async () => {\n      const done: string[] = []\n      for (const [index, row] of queue.entries()) {\n        setCursor({ name: row.id, index: index + 1, total: queue.length })\n        try {\n          const result = await update(row.id)\n          // The update landed; when this process cannot load it, the run still\n          // counts as applied and continues, and the panel names the restart.\n          if (result.restartRequired.length > 0) {\n            setRestartRequired(current => [...current, { id: row.id, version: result.plugin.version }])\n          }\n        } catch (reason) {\n          // Stop at the first failure: the remaining rows stay listed with their\n          // versions, so the user sees exactly what did not go through.\n          setError(t('failed', { reason: messageOf(reason) }))\n          break\n        }\n        done.push(row.id)\n        setApplied([...done])\n        setRows(current => current.filter(item => item.id !== row.id))\n      }\n      setCursor(undefined)\n    })().finally(() => {\n      busyRef.current = false\n      setPhase('idle')\n    })\n  }\n\n  /** Ask the host how it would restart, then show the confirmation that matches. */\n  const onAskRestart = (): void => {\n    if (busyRef.current) return\n    busyRef.current = true\n    setError(undefined)\n    void restartPlan().then(mode => {\n      setPlan(mode)\n      setPanel('restart')\n    }).catch(reason => {\n      setError(t('failed', { reason: messageOf(reason) }))\n      setPanel('list')\n    }).finally(() => {\n      busyRef.current = false\n    })\n  }\n\n  const onRestart = (): void => {\n    if (busyRef.current) return\n    busyRef.current = true\n    setError(undefined)\n    void restart().then(mode => {\n      setRestartMode(mode)\n      setPlan(undefined)\n      setPanel('none')\n    }).catch(reason => {\n      setError(t('failed', { reason: messageOf(reason) }))\n    }).finally(() => {\n      busyRef.current = false\n    })\n  }\n\n  const shellProps = {\n    'data-dsh-plugin': 'plugin-manager',\n    'data-dsh-part': 'update-toolbar',\n    'data-update-toolbar': true,\n  } as const\n\n  if (!isLoopback) {\n    return (\n      <div className={css.toolbar} {...shellProps} data-state=\"local-only\">\n        <button type=\"button\" className={css.toolbarButton} disabled title={t('localOnlyBody')}>\n          {t('checkUpdates')}\n        </button>\n      </div>\n    )\n  }\n\n  const busy = phase !== 'idle'\n  /** One alert line, rendered in whichever flyout is open when it appears. */\n  const errorLine = error === undefined\n    ? null\n    : <p className={css.error} role=\"alert\" data-update-error>{error}</p>\n  /** What is still pending after a partial run (the applied rows leave the list). */\n  const remaining = found - applied.length\n  const summary = cursor !== undefined\n    ? t('updatingAll', { name: cursor.name, index: String(cursor.index), total: String(cursor.total) })\n    : remaining > 0\n      ? t('updatesAvailable', { count: String(remaining) })\n      : applied.length > 0\n        ? t('updateAllDone')\n        : t('noUpdates')\n\n  return (\n    <div className={css.toolbar} {...shellProps} data-state={restartMode ?? phase} aria-busy={busy}>\n      <button type=\"button\" className={css.toolbarButton} data-update-check disabled={busy} onClick={onCheck}>\n        {phase === 'checking' ? t('checking') : t('checkUpdates')}\n      </button>\n\n      {checked && (\n        <button\n          type=\"button\"\n          className={css.toolbarSummary}\n          data-update-summary\n          data-pending={pending.length}\n          aria-expanded={panel === 'list'}\n          onClick={() => { setPanel(panel === 'list' ? 'none' : 'list') }}\n        >\n          {summary}\n        </button>\n      )}\n\n      <button\n        type=\"button\"\n        className={applied.length > 0 ? `${css.toolbarButton} ${css.primary}` : css.toolbarButton}\n        data-update-restart\n        data-restart-pending={applied.length}\n        disabled={busy || restartMode === 'relaunch'}\n        onClick={() => { if (panel === 'restart') { setPanel('none'); setPlan(undefined); return } onAskRestart() }}\n      >\n        {restartMode === 'relaunch' ? t('restarting') : t('restartNow')}\n      </button>\n\n      {restartMode !== undefined && panel !== 'restart' && (\n        <span className={css.toolbarHint} role=\"status\" data-update-restart-hint={restartMode}>\n          {restartMode === 'shell' ? t('restartDesktopHint') : restartMode === 'manual' ? t('restartManualHint') : t('restartRelaunchHint')}\n        </span>\n      )}\n\n      {panel === 'list' && (\n        <div className={css.panel} data-update-panel role=\"group\" aria-label={t('updatesPanelTitle')}>\n          {errorLine}\n          {applied.length > 0 && <p className={css.ok} data-update-applied>{t('updateAllDone')}</p>}\n          {restartRequired.length > 0 && (\n            <ul className={css.restartRequired} data-update-restart-required>\n              {restartRequired.map(item => (\n                <li key={item.id} className={css.panelRow} data-update-restart-row={item.id}>\n                  <span className={css.panelName}>{item.id}</span>\n                  <span className={css.restartRequiredLine}>{t('updateRestartRequired', { version: item.version })}</span>\n                </li>\n              ))}\n            </ul>\n          )}\n          {rows.length === 0 && applied.length === 0 && error === undefined && <p className={css.hint}>{t('noUpdates')}</p>}\n          {rows.length > 0 && (\n            <ul className={css.panelList}>\n              {rows.map(row => {\n                // One verdict per row, read once: the badge, its copy and the\n                // bulk action's exclusion all come from the same answer.\n                const gate = dshGateOf(row)\n                return (\n                  <li key={row.id} className={css.panelRow} data-update-row={row.id} data-compatible={gate === 'open' ? 'yes' : 'no'}>\n                    <span className={css.panelName}>{row.id}</span>\n                    <span className={css.panelVersion}>{row.current} → {row.latest}</span>\n                    {gate === 'open' ? null : (\n                      <span className={css.compatBlocked} data-update-row-compat-reason={gate}>\n                        {row.requiresDsh !== undefined\n                          ? t(gate === 'unverified' ? 'updateUnverifiedDsh' : 'updateBlockedDsh', {\n                            min: displayMinimumVersion(row.requiresDsh),\n                          })\n                          : t('updateUnverifiedDshUnknownRange')}\n                      </span>\n                    )}\n                  </li>\n                )\n              })}\n            </ul>\n          )}\n          <div className={css.panelActions}>\n            {pending.length > 0 && (\n              <button type=\"button\" className={`${css.button} ${css.primary}`} data-update-all disabled={busy} onClick={onUpdateAll}>\n                {phase === 'updating' ? t('updating') : t('updateAll', { count: String(pending.length) })}\n              </button>\n            )}\n            {applied.length > 0 && (\n              <button type=\"button\" className={`${css.button} ${css.primary}`} data-update-panel-restart disabled={busy} onClick={onAskRestart}>\n                {t('restartNow')}\n              </button>\n            )}\n          </div>\n          <p className={css.hint}>{t('thirdPartyOnly')}</p>\n        </div>\n      )}\n\n      {panel === 'restart' && (\n        <div className={css.panel} data-update-restart-panel data-restart-plan={plan} role=\"group\" aria-label={t('restartNow')}>\n          {errorLine}\n          <p className={css.hint} data-restart-plan-hint={plan}>\n            {plan === 'shell' ? t('restartPlanShell') : plan === 'manual' ? t('restartPlanManual') : t('restartPlanRelaunch')}\n          </p>\n          {plan === 'shell' && <p className={css.hint}>{t('restartShellWarning')}</p>}\n          <div className={css.panelActions}>\n            <button type=\"button\" className={css.button} data-restart-cancel onClick={() => { setPanel('none'); setPlan(undefined) }}>\n              {t('cancel')}\n            </button>\n            {plan !== 'manual' && (\n              <button\n                type=\"button\"\n                className={`${css.button} ${css.primary}`}\n                data-restart-confirm\n                onClick={onRestart}\n              >\n                {t('restartConfirm')}\n              </button>\n            )}\n          </div>\n        </div>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "packages/dsh-plugin-manager/src/client/index.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Plugin-manager browser half: contributes the package's one remaining\n * surface — the check-for-updates block on the official Plugins page — and\n * provides the dual-channel face as the `'pluginManager'` cordis service for\n * sibling client plugins.\n *\n * It is dual-channel: on runtimes with the official installer services\n * (DSHCode, the 1.0.4 checkout web) every operation rides the official\n * `/plugin-installer` and `/plugin-control` loopback RPC channels (the single\n * writer); on the npm-published web runtime those channels do not exist, so the\n * same face falls back to this package's own loopback HTTP gateway, which\n * spawns the official CLI for writes. Neither the patch nor service consumers\n * know which mode the face runs in.\n *\n * The package used to register its own \"Plugin manager\" tab into the official\n * Plugins settings section (`settings.plugins.tab`). Installing, uninstalling\n * and enabling moved to the official page long ago, and the tab's remaining\n * half was UI no official page renders; the tab is gone and its one genuinely\n * missing capability — comparing an installed plugin against its registry\n * source, with the DSH-runtime compatibility gate — now renders inside the\n * official page through the `plugins.detail.section` seat it declares.\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager/client\n */\n\n// Type-only: pulls the locale plugin's Context merge (ctx.locale).\nimport type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale/client'\n// Type-only: pulls the renderer plugin's Context merge (ctx.slots, the\n// registry this package registers its contribution into).\nimport type {} from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer/client'\nimport type { Context as ClientContext } from '@deepseek-ai/cordis'\nimport type { ConnectionHandle } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection/client'\nimport { PluginUpdatePatch, type PluginUpdatePatchInjected } from './PluginUpdatePatch.tsx'\nimport { mountPluginListToolbar } from './plugin-toolbar-mount.tsx'\nimport { en, zh, type PluginManagerKey } from './locales.ts'\nimport {\n  parseFailuresSnapshot,\n  parseInstallStatus,\n  parseInstalledPlugin,\n  parsePluginList,\n  parseRestartMode,\n  parseRestartRequired,\n  parseUpdateList,\n  type InstalledPluginItem,\n  type InstallProgressItem,\n  type PluginFailuresSnapshot,\n  type PluginUpdateItem,\n  type PluginUpdateResult,\n  type RestartMode,\n} from '../core/protocol.ts'\nimport { PLUGIN_MANAGER_SERVICE, type PluginManagerService } from '../core/service.ts'\nimport { reportDailyHeartbeat } from './telemetry.ts'\n\ndeclare module '@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-slots' {\n  interface LocaleNamespaceMap {\n    /** Copy for the check-for-updates patch. */\n    'settings.pluginManager': PluginManagerKey\n  }\n}\n\nconst NS = 'settings.pluginManager'\nconst CHANNEL = '/plugin-installer'\nconst LIST_ENDPOINT = 'list'\nconst INSTALL_ENDPOINT = 'install'\nconst UPDATE_ENDPOINT = 'update'\nconst UNINSTALL_ENDPOINT = 'uninstall'\nconst SET_ENABLED_ENDPOINT = 'set-enabled'\nconst CHECK_UPDATES_ENDPOINT = 'check-updates'\nconst RESTART_ENDPOINT = 'restart'\nconst STATUS_ENDPOINT = 'status'\nconst FAILURES_ENDPOINT = 'failures'\n\n// DOCUMENT-RELATIVE (issue #1707): the GUI is served with `<base href=\"./\">`,\n// so a sub-path deployment resolves the gateway prefix against its entry\n// directory rather than the origin root.\nconst GATEWAY_PREFIX = 'api/plugin-manager'\n/** Gateway job polling cadence. */\nconst JOB_POLL_MS = 500\n/** Gateway job wait ceiling (the host add deadline is six minutes). */\nconst JOB_WAIT_MS = 7 * 60_000\n\n/** Services required by the patch registration and both channels. */\nexport const inject = ['slots', 'locale', 'connection']\n\n/** The gateway job wire shape served by /status. */\ninterface GatewayJobWire {\n  phase: 'running' | 'done' | 'error'\n  plugin?: unknown\n  error?: string\n  /**\n   * Bundles the job applied but this process has not loaded (the host read\n   * `application: 'restart-required'` from the official manager). Optional and\n   * untyped here: it is read through {@link parseRestartRequired}, which\n   * degrades an unusable value to \"no restart needed\" instead of rejecting an\n   * update that already landed.\n   */\n  restartRequired?: unknown\n}\n\n/**\n * The face the update patch and the `'pluginManager'` cordis service share:\n * the patch's wire surface plus the cross-plugin service contract. The gateway\n * host still records install conflicts and boot failures; no client surface\n * consumes either since the tab left, so neither is on this face.\n */\nexport type PluginManagerFace = PluginUpdatePatchInjected & PluginManagerService & {\n  /**\n   * Restart DSH so an applied plugin update is loaded. Always rides this\n   * package's own loopback route: neither official channel\n   * (`/plugin-installer`, `/plugin-control`) has a restart method, and the\n   * route answers how the restart was carried out (in-place relaunch, or a\n   * packaged Desktop shell that owns the process tree). See host/restart.ts.\n   */\n  restart: () => Promise<RestartMode>\n  /**\n   * Read how a restart would be carried out without triggering it (the same\n   * route's plan read). The toolbar words its confirmation from this, so a\n   * packaged Desktop host can say what its system dialog will do instead of\n   * surprising the user with it.\n   */\n  restartPlan: () => Promise<RestartMode>\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the dual-channel face once: official-channel and gateway-channel\n * implementations, the mode detection that picks between them, and the\n * change-notification listener set. The returned face is both the update\n * patch's injected props and the value provided as the\n * `'pluginManager'` cordis service.\n * @param ctx - the client context (connection).\n * @returns the shared face.\n */\nexport function createPluginManagerFace(ctx: ClientContext): PluginManagerFace {\n  const connection = ctx.get('connection') as ConnectionHandle\n\n  // Official channel implementations.\n\n  const call = async (endpoint: string, payload: unknown): Promise<unknown> => {\n    const result = await connection.rpc.call(CHANNEL, endpoint, payload)\n    if (!result.ok) {\n      throw new Error(`plugin-installer ${endpoint} failed: ${result.error.code}: ${result.error.message}`)\n    }\n    return result.value\n  }\n  const official = {\n    list: async (): Promise<InstalledPluginItem[]> => parsePluginList(await call(LIST_ENDPOINT, {})),\n    install: async (spec: string): Promise<InstalledPluginItem> => parseInstalledPlugin(await call(INSTALL_ENDPOINT, { spec })),\n    update: async (id: string): Promise<PluginUpdateResult> => ({\n      plugin: parseInstalledPlugin(await call(UPDATE_ENDPOINT, { id })),\n      // The official installer channel reports no restart fact: it owns the\n      // load itself, so an applied update there is one this process serves.\n      restartRequired: [],\n    }),\n    uninstall: async (id: string): Promise<InstalledPluginItem[]> => parsePluginList(await call(UNINSTALL_ENDPOINT, { id })),\n    setEnabled: async (id: string, enabled: boolean): Promise<InstalledPluginItem> =>\n      parseInstalledPlugin(await call(SET_ENABLED_ENDPOINT, { id, enabled })),\n    checkUpdates: async (): Promise<PluginUpdateItem[]> => parseUpdateList(await call(CHECK_UPDATES_ENDPOINT, {})),\n    status: async (): Promise<InstallProgressItem> => parseInstallStatus(await call(STATUS_ENDPOINT, {})),\n    failures: async (): Promise<PluginFailuresSnapshot> => parseFailuresSnapshot(await call(FAILURES_ENDPOINT, {})),\n  }\n\n  // Gateway channel implementations.\n\n  const gatewayJson = async (path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<unknown> => {\n    const response = await fetch(path, {\n      ...init,\n      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json', ...init?.headers },\n    })\n    if (response.status === 403) {\n      throw new Error('plugin-manager: plugin management is only available from a local browser')\n    }\n    if (!response.ok) {\n      const body = await response.json().catch(() => ({})) as { error?: string }\n      throw new Error(body.error ?? `plugin-manager: gateway ${path} failed: HTTP ${String(response.status)}`)\n    }\n    return response.json()\n  }\n\n  /** Wait for one gateway job to settle, returning its wire state. */\n  const waitJob = async (jobId: string): Promise<GatewayJobWire> => {\n    const deadline = Date.now() + JOB_WAIT_MS\n    for (;;) {\n      const body = await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/status?job=${encodeURIComponent(jobId)}`) as { job?: GatewayJobWire }\n      const job = body.job\n      if (job === undefined) throw new Error('plugin-manager: gateway job vanished')\n      if (job.phase === 'done') return job\n      if (job.phase === 'error') throw new Error(job.error ?? 'plugin-manager: gateway job failed')\n      if (Date.now() > deadline) throw new Error('plugin-manager: gateway job timed out')\n      await new Promise(resolve => { setTimeout(resolve, JOB_POLL_MS) })\n    }\n  }\n\n  /** Whether a gateway install/remove is in flight (drives the progress row). */\n  let gatewayInflight = false\n\n  const gateway = {\n    list: async (): Promise<InstalledPluginItem[]> =>\n      parsePluginList(await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/list`)),\n    install: async (spec: string): Promise<InstalledPluginItem> => {\n      gatewayInflight = true\n      try {\n        const started = await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/install`, {\n          method: 'POST',\n          body: JSON.stringify({ spec }),\n        }) as { jobId?: string }\n        if (started.jobId === undefined) throw new Error('plugin-manager: gateway install returned no job')\n        const job = await waitJob(started.jobId)\n        return parseInstalledPlugin({ plugin: job.plugin })\n      } finally {\n        gatewayInflight = false\n      }\n    },\n    update: async (id: string): Promise<PluginUpdateResult> => {\n      gatewayInflight = true\n      try {\n        const started = await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/update`, {\n          method: 'POST',\n          body: JSON.stringify({ id }),\n        }) as { jobId?: string }\n        if (started.jobId === undefined) throw new Error('plugin-manager: gateway update returned no job')\n        const job = await waitJob(started.jobId)\n        return {\n          plugin: parseInstalledPlugin({ plugin: job.plugin }),\n          // The job is done either way; this is the difference between an\n          // update this process serves and one only a restart loads.\n          restartRequired: parseRestartRequired(job.restartRequired),\n        }\n      } finally {\n        gatewayInflight = false\n      }\n    },\n    uninstall: async (id: string): Promise<InstalledPluginItem[]> => {\n      gatewayInflight = true\n      try {\n        const started = await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/remove`, {\n          method: 'POST',\n          body: JSON.stringify({ id }),\n        }) as { jobId?: string }\n        if (started.jobId === undefined) throw new Error('plugin-manager: gateway remove returned no job')\n        await waitJob(started.jobId)\n        return gateway.list()\n      } finally {\n        gatewayInflight = false\n      }\n    },\n    setEnabled: async (id: string, enabled: boolean): Promise<InstalledPluginItem> =>\n      parseInstalledPlugin(await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/set-enabled`, {\n        method: 'POST',\n        body: JSON.stringify({ id, enabled }),\n      })),\n    checkUpdates: async (): Promise<PluginUpdateItem[]> =>\n      parseUpdateList(await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/check-updates`)),\n    status: async (): Promise<InstallProgressItem> =>\n      gatewayInflight ? { kind: 'install', stage: 'download' } : { kind: 'idle', stage: 'fetch' },\n    failures: async (): Promise<PluginFailuresSnapshot> =>\n      parseFailuresSnapshot(await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/failures`)),\n    // Restart has no official-channel counterpart, so this route is the one\n    // call that is always the gateway's, whichever mode the face runs in. The\n    // GET-shaped call is the plan read: no state changes, no process exits.\n    restartPlan: async (): Promise<RestartMode> =>\n      parseRestartMode(await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/${RESTART_ENDPOINT}`)),\n    restart: async (): Promise<RestartMode> =>\n      parseRestartMode(await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/${RESTART_ENDPOINT}`, { method: 'POST' })),\n  }\n\n  // Mode selection.\n\n  let modePromise: Promise<'official' | 'gateway'> | undefined\n  const ensureMode = (): Promise<'official' | 'gateway'> => {\n    if (modePromise === undefined) {\n      modePromise = (async () => {\n        // Prefer the host verdict: the gateway's /mode route reports whether\n        // the official installer channels exist, so the direct channel probe\n        // below (which 405s into the browser console on the npm web runtime)\n        // only runs when the host half is absent or explicitly returns null\n        // for a desktop runtime whose services are registered in-process.\n        try {\n          const mode = await gatewayJson(`${GATEWAY_PREFIX}/mode`) as { official?: boolean | null }\n          if (mode.official === true) return 'official' as const\n          if (mode.official === false) return 'gateway' as const\n        } catch {\n          // Host half absent (an official runtime without a boot profile):\n          // fall back to the direct channel probe.\n        }\n        try {\n          const result = await connection.rpc.call(CHANNEL, LIST_ENDPOINT, {})\n          return result.ok ? 'official' as const : 'gateway' as const\n        } catch {\n          return 'gateway' as const\n        }\n      })()\n    }\n    return modePromise\n  }\n\n  // Change notification.\n\n  /** Listeners subscribed through onChange; fired after successful mutations. */\n  const listeners = new Set<() => void>()\n  /** Notify every listener; one listener throwing never breaks the others. */\n  const notifyChange = (): void => {\n    for (const listener of [...listeners]) {\n      try {\n        listener()\n      } catch {\n        // A consumer's listener failure is its own; keep notifying the rest.\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  // The shared face.\n\n  return {\n    isLoopback: connection.isLoopback,\n    list: async () => (await ensureMode()) === 'official' ? official.list() : gateway.list(),\n    install: async spec => {\n      const item = await ((await ensureMode()) === 'official' ? official.install(spec) : gateway.install(spec))\n      notifyChange()\n      return item\n    },\n    update: async id => {\n      const item = await ((await ensureMode()) === 'official' ? official.update(id) : gateway.update(id))\n      notifyChange()\n      return item\n    },\n    uninstall: async id => {\n      const rows = await ((await ensureMode()) === 'official' ? official.uninstall(id) : gateway.uninstall(id))\n      notifyChange()\n      return rows\n    },\n    setEnabled: async (id, enabled) => {\n      const item = await ((await ensureMode()) === 'official' ? official.setEnabled(id, enabled) : gateway.setEnabled(id, enabled))\n      notifyChange()\n      return item\n    },\n    checkUpdates: async () => (await ensureMode()) === 'official' ? official.checkUpdates() : gateway.checkUpdates(),\n    restartPlan: () => gateway.restartPlan(),\n    restart: () => gateway.restart(),\n    status: async () => (await ensureMode()) === 'official' ? official.status() : gateway.status(),\n    failures: async () => (await ensureMode()) === 'official' ? official.failures() : gateway.failures(),\n    onChange: cb => {\n      listeners.add(cb)\n      return () => { listeners.delete(cb) }\n    },\n  }\n}\n\n/** Contribute the check-for-updates patch and provide the shared face. */\nexport function apply(ctx: ClientContext): void {\n  // Anonymous install heartbeat (docs/telemetry.md): one beat per browser per\n  // UTC day, package name only, silent failure.\n  reportDailyHeartbeat([{ name: '@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager' }])\n\n  ctx.effect(() => {\n    try {\n      return ctx.locale.register(NS, { zh, en })\n    } catch {\n      return () => {}\n    }\n  }, 'plugin-manager: dictionaries')\n\n  // Built once: the patch and the 'pluginManager' cordis service share one\n  // face, so consumers observe exactly the mutations the patch performs.\n  const face = createPluginManagerFace(ctx)\n  try {\n    if (!ctx.get(PLUGIN_MANAGER_SERVICE)) {\n      ctx.provide(PLUGIN_MANAGER_SERVICE, face)\n    }\n  } catch {\n    // ignore duplicate provide\n  }\n\n  // The list-level toolbar rides the page's own \"Installed\" heading: the\n  // official page declares no seat beside it, so the entry is inserted into\n  // the heading element itself and tracks the page through the shared body\n  // mutation hub. Its translate function is rebuilt on every render so a\n  // language switch reaches copy that no slot outlet owns.\n  ctx.effect(() => {\n    try {\n      return mountPluginListToolbar({\n        props: () => ({\n          isLoopback: face.isLoopback,\n          checkUpdates: face.checkUpdates,\n          update: face.update,\n          restartPlan: face.restartPlan,\n          restart: face.restart,\n          t: ctx.locale.bind(NS),\n        }),\n        subscribe: listener => ctx.locale.subscribe(listener),\n      })\n    } catch {\n      return () => {}\n    }\n  }, 'plugin-manager: update toolbar')\n\n  // The official Plugins page declares this seat on its main-panel entry and\n  // renders one section per contribution on each bundle / row / plugin page;\n  // `inject` waits for that declaration, exactly like the family plugin cards\n  // that register into `plugins.bundle.config`.\n  ctx.slots.inject('plugins.detail.section', () => {\n    try {\n      return ctx.slots.register({\n        name: 'plugins.detail.section',\n        id: 'family-update-check',\n        order: 30,\n        locale: NS,\n        inject: () => face,\n      }, PluginUpdatePatch)\n    } catch {\n      return () => {}\n    }\n  })\n}\n"

      "path": "packages/dsh-plugin-manager/src/client/plugin-toolbar-mount.tsx",
      "content": "/**\n * Mounting the update toolbar beside the official Plugins page's \"Installed\"\n * heading.\n *\n * The page renders that heading itself — `<section data-plugin-group=\"bundles\">\n * <div class=\"groupHead\"><h3>Installed</h3><span>7</span></div>…` — and declares\n * no seat next to it: its extension points are `plugins.detail.*` (per page),\n * `plugins.bundle.config` / `plugins.row.config` / `plugins.item` (configuration\n * entries) and `plugins.bundle.activation`. A list-level action therefore has\n * to be inserted into the page's own chrome, the same way the sidebar foot card\n * is inserted above the Settings row.\n *\n * The container is a plain element carrying its own React root, so it can never\n * disturb the page's reconciliation, and it re-seats itself through the\n * page-wide body-mutation hub: a re-render that relocates or drops the heading\n * is followed on the next frame, and a panel switch that unmounts the list\n * simply detaches the container until the list returns.\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager/client\n */\n\nimport { createElement } from 'react'\nimport { createRoot, type Root } from 'react-dom/client'\nimport { subscribeBodyInvalidations } from './body-mutations.ts'\nimport { PluginListToolbar, type PluginListToolbarProps } from './PluginListToolbar.tsx'\nimport css from './plugin-manager.module.css'\n\n/** Stable attribute identifying the injected container (mount idempotency). */\nexport const TOOLBAR_MOUNT_SELECTOR = '[data-dsh-plugin-manager-toolbar]'\n\n/** Toolbar props without the translate function, which is rebuilt per render. */\nexport type PluginListToolbarMountInput = Omit<PluginListToolbarProps, 't'> & {\n  /** Translate in the namespace, read on every render so a language switch lands. */\n  t: PluginListToolbarProps['t']\n}\n\n/** The mount's inputs. */\nexport interface PluginToolbarMountOptions {\n  /** Build the toolbar props; called on mount and on every locale change. */\n  props: () => PluginListToolbarMountInput\n  /** Locale change subscription (ctx.locale.subscribe); re-renders the toolbar. */\n  subscribe?: (listener: () => void) => () => void\n}\n\n/**\n * The official page's \"Installed\" group heading, when it is mounted. Class\n * names are CSS-module hashes in the official bundle, so the seat is found\n * through the page's own data attributes plus DOM position.\n * @returns the heading element to append into, or undefined off the list view.\n */\nexport function toolbarSeat(): HTMLElement | undefined {\n  const page = document.querySelector('[data-plugin-panel]')\n  const group = page?.querySelector('[data-plugin-group=\"bundles\"]')\n  const head = group?.firstElementChild\n  return head instanceof HTMLElement ? head : undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * Mount the toolbar into the Installed heading.\n * @param options - props factory and the optional locale subscription.\n * @returns disposer removing the container, its observers and its React root.\n */\nexport function mountPluginListToolbar(options: PluginToolbarMountOptions): () => void {\n  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return () => {}\n  // DOM-level idempotency: whatever path mounted a toolbar before this call\n  // (a duplicated apply, an HMR re-injection), never mount a second one.\n  if (document.querySelector(TOOLBAR_MOUNT_SELECTOR) !== null) return () => {}\n\n  const container = document.createElement('div')\n  container.setAttribute('data-dsh-plugin-manager-toolbar', '')\n  container.className = css.mount\n  const root: Root = createRoot(container)\n  const render = (): void => {\n    root.render(createElement(PluginListToolbar, options.props()))\n  }\n  render()\n\n  /** Keep the container inside the heading; detach while the list is away. */\n  const place = (): void => {\n    const seat = toolbarSeat()\n    if (seat === undefined) {\n      container.remove()\n      return\n    }\n    if (container.parentElement !== seat) seat.append(container)\n  }\n  place()\n\n  const unsubscribeBody = subscribeBodyInvalidations(place)\n  const unsubscribeLocale = options.subscribe === undefined ? ((): void => {}) : options.subscribe(render)\n\n  return () => {\n    unsubscribeBody()\n    unsubscribeLocale()\n    root.unmount()\n    container.remove()\n  }\n}\n"

      "path": "packages/dsh-plugin-manager/src/client/telemetry.ts",
      "content": "// Generated by scripts/sync-shared.mjs from shared/client/telemetry.ts. Do not edit this copy; edit the shared source and run \"node scripts/sync-shared.mjs\".\n/**\n * Anonymous install telemetry shared by the DSH Web UI family plugins.\n *\n * Once per UTC day per browser, each wired plugin sends one heartbeat to\n * the dsh-market edge API listing its package name (and version when known).\n * The payload carries no conversation data and no identifiers beyond a random\n * UUID generated in localStorage; the server hashes it with a deployment salt\n * before storage and never persists IP addresses. Sends are fire-and-forget:\n * failures stay silent and simply retry on a later mount or day. Frames where\n * storage is unavailable report nothing.\n *\n * The family-wide opt-out and the browser's Do Not Track signal both suppress\n * the heartbeat; the Web Plugins settings switch writes the same localStorage\n * key. The system is documented in docs/telemetry.md.\n */\n\nexport type TelemetryChannel = 'market' | 'npm' | 'unknown'\n\nexport interface TelemetryItem {\n  /** npm package name or asset id, e.g. \"@linxin666/dsh-pet\" or \"skin:harbor\". */\n  name: string\n  /** Installed version when known; omitted otherwise. */\n  version?: string\n  /** Install channel when determinable (market = Workshop install). */\n  channel?: TelemetryChannel\n}\n\n/** localStorage key carrying the family-wide telemetry opt-out ('1' = off). */\nexport const TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY = 'dsh-web-ui-telemetry-opt-out'\n\nconst VISITOR_KEY = 'dsh-web-ui-telemetry-visitor'\nconst DAY_KEY_PREFIX = 'dsh-web-ui-telemetry-day:'\nconst ENDPOINT = 'https://dsh-market.com/api/telemetry/event'\n\n// Baked into each client bundle by shared/tsdown.client.ts (the package's own\n// package.json version at build time). Undefined in dev/test builds.\ndeclare const __DSH_PKG_VERSION__: string | undefined\n\n/** The building package's version, when the bundle carries it. */\nfunction bakedVersion(): string | undefined {\n  try {\n    return typeof __DSH_PKG_VERSION__ === 'string' && __DSH_PKG_VERSION__ !== ''\n      ? __DSH_PKG_VERSION__\n      : undefined\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  }\n}\n\n/** Whether the user switched the family-wide opt-out on (reads storage only). */\nexport function isTelemetryOptedOut(): boolean {\n  try {\n    return localStorage.getItem(TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY) === '1'\n  } catch {\n    // Storage unavailable: there is no stored opt-out to honour.\n    return false\n  }\n}\n\n/** Turn the family-wide opt-out on or off (writing '1' / removing the key); never throws. */\nexport function setTelemetryOptedOut(optedOut: boolean): void {\n  try {\n    if (optedOut) localStorage.setItem(TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY, '1')\n    else localStorage.removeItem(TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT_KEY)\n  } catch {\n    // Storage unavailable: the preference cannot be persisted on this machine.\n  }\n}\n\n/** Whether the browser itself asks not to be tracked; a failed read means no signal. */\nfunction doNotTrackRequested(): boolean {\n  try {\n    // '1' per the DNT header spec, 'yes' from older Firefox builds.\n    return navigator.doNotTrack === '1' || navigator.doNotTrack === 'yes'\n  } catch {\n    return false\n  }\n}\n\n/** Whether a heartbeat must be suppressed right now: opt-out stored, or the browser asks not to be tracked. */\nexport function isTelemetrySuppressed(): boolean {\n  return isTelemetryOptedOut() || doNotTrackRequested()\n}\n\n/** Read or lazily create the anonymous visitor id; null when storage is unavailable. */\nfunction visitorId(): string | null {\n  try {\n    const existing = localStorage.getItem(VISITOR_KEY)\n    if (existing && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,64}$/.test(existing)) return existing\n    const fresh = crypto.randomUUID().replaceAll('-', '')\n    localStorage.setItem(VISITOR_KEY, fresh)\n    return fresh\n  } catch {\n    // Storage unavailable (privacy mode, sandboxed frame): report nothing.\n    return null\n  }\n}\n\n/** Drop stale per-day dedup keys so localStorage does not grow forever. */\nfunction pruneDayKeys(today: string): void {\n  try {\n    for (let index = localStorage.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {\n      const key = localStorage.key(index)\n      if (key !== null && key.startsWith(DAY_KEY_PREFIX) && key !== DAY_KEY_PREFIX + today) {\n        localStorage.removeItem(key)\n      }\n    }\n  } catch { /* best effort */ }\n}\n\n/**\n * Fire the daily heartbeat for the given items at most once per UTC day per\n * browser. Never throws and never blocks the caller. Items without an explicit\n * version inherit the bundle's baked build version.\n */\nexport function reportDailyHeartbeat(items: readonly TelemetryItem[]): void {\n  try {\n    // First guard: a stored opt-out or the browser's Do Not Track stops every\n    // read below from minting an id, marking the day, or reaching the network.\n    if (isTelemetrySuppressed()) return\n    if (items.length === 0) return\n    const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10)\n    // Automation contexts (CDP-driven QA browsers, fresh isolated profiles)\n    // mint a new visitor id per run and would inflate instance counts.\n    if (navigator.webdriver) return\n    if (localStorage.getItem(DAY_KEY_PREFIX + today) !== null) return\n    const visitor = visitorId()\n    if (visitor === null) return\n    pruneDayKeys(today)\n    const payloadItems = items.map((item) => {\n      const out: Record<string, string> = { name: item.name }\n      const version = item.version ?? bakedVersion()\n      if (version !== undefined) out.version = version\n      if (item.channel !== undefined) out.channel = item.channel\n      return out\n    })\n    const body = JSON.stringify({ kind: 'heartbeat', visitor, items: payloadItems })\n    void fetch(ENDPOINT, {\n      method: 'POST',\n      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },\n      body,\n      keepalive: true,\n    }).then((response) => {\n      // Mark the day only after an accepted send, so offline browsers retry\n      // on a later mount instead of going dark until tomorrow.\n      if (response.ok) localStorage.setItem(DAY_KEY_PREFIX + today, '1')\n    }).catch(() => { /* unreachable endpoint: stay silent */ })\n  } catch { /* never break the host UI over telemetry */ }\n}\n"

      "path": "packages/dsh-plugin-manager/src/core/updates.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Which update rows the list-level toolbar may act on. Pure, shared by the\n * browser half (the toolbar) and its tests: the host answers with every\n * installed package whose registry source serves a newer release, and the\n * policy of what may be updated in bulk lives here rather than in the host,\n * so the same rows stay available to the per-page update block.\n *\n * Two filters:\n *\n * - **Third-party only.** A package published under the `@deepseek-ai/` scope\n *   ships with DSH itself: its version is chosen by the running installation,\n *   the official page says an upgrade arrives by upgrading DSH, and a\n *   plugin-initiated `pnpm add` of such a package can pull a release the runtime was\n *   never tested against. The bulk action therefore never touches it.\n * - **Compatibility gate.** An update whose manifest declares a DSH minimum the\n *   running host does not satisfy is listed (the user may still upgrade DSH)\n *   but cannot be applied: the host would refuse it with 412 anyway.\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager/core\n */\n\nimport type { PluginUpdateItem } from './protocol.ts'\n\n/** The npm scope DSH's own packages are published under. */\nexport const OFFICIAL_SCOPE = '@deepseek-ai/'\n\n/** Whether a package id is a third-party plugin rather than a DSH-shipped one. */\nexport function isThirdPartyPlugin(id: string): boolean {\n  return !id.startsWith(OFFICIAL_SCOPE)\n}\n\n/** The third-party update rows, in host order. */\nexport function thirdPartyUpdates(items: readonly PluginUpdateItem[]): PluginUpdateItem[] {\n  return items.filter(item => isThirdPartyPlugin(item.id))\n}\n\n/** Whether the running DSH host satisfies the row's declared minimum. */\nexport function isUpdateApplicable(item: PluginUpdateItem): boolean {\n  return item.compatible !== false\n}\n\n/** The third-party rows this runtime can actually apply. */\nexport function applicableUpdates(items: readonly PluginUpdateItem[]): PluginUpdateItem[] {\n  return thirdPartyUpdates(items).filter(isUpdateApplicable)\n}\n"
