      "path": "packages/dsh-plugin-manager/src/core/version.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Version parsing plus the requirement reader for the update compatibility\n * check. The declared minimum lives in the published package manifest under\n * `dsh.engines.dsh`, falling back to the top-level `engines.dsh` and then to\n * the `@deepseek-ai/dsh` peer; the range forms a manifest may use are the\n * full node-semver range grammar.\n *\n * This module is shared by both halves and therefore stays free of `semver`,\n * which is a node package: it parses and compares a single `X.Y.Z[-pre]`\n * version, which is all the browser half needs to render a declared range\n * (`displayMinimumVersion`) and all the host half needs to accept a probed\n * host version (`parseDshVersion`). The range verdict itself lives in the\n * host-only `../host/dsh-compat.ts`, which evaluates the declaration with\n * `semver.satisfies(host, range, { includePrerelease: true })` — the exact\n * call the official boot gate makes, so `||`, `^`, `~`, multi-comparator\n * and x-ranges all decide the same way here as they do at boot.\n *\n * Everything here is pure and tolerant of untrusted input: a malformed value\n * means \"cannot verify\", which the callers treat as a fail-closed verdict\n * when a requirement was declared (issue #754).\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager/core\n */\n\n/** One parsed DSH host or package version. */\nexport interface DshVersion {\n  major: number\n  minor: number\n  patch: number\n  /** Prerelease identifiers, numeric identifiers kept as numbers (semver order). */\n  prerelease: readonly (number | string)[]\n}\n\nconst VERSION_PATTERN = /^v?(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)\\.(\\d+)(?:-([0-9A-Za-z.-]+))?$/\n\n/**\n * Parse a DSH host or package version string.\n * @param value - e.g. `0.1.0-rc.8`, `v1.2.3`.\n * @returns the parsed version, or undefined when malformed.\n */\nexport function parseDshVersion(value: string): DshVersion | undefined {\n  const match = VERSION_PATTERN.exec(value.trim())\n  if (match === null) return undefined\n  const prereleaseParts = match[4] === undefined ? [] : match[4].split('.')\n  if (prereleaseParts.some(part => part === '')) return undefined\n  return {\n    major: Number(match[1]),\n    minor: Number(match[2]),\n    patch: Number(match[3]),\n    prerelease: prereleaseParts.map(part => /^\\d+$/.test(part) ? Number(part) : part),\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Compare two version strings by semver order (a release is newer than any\n * prerelease of the same tuple).\n * @returns -1 / 0 / 1, or undefined when either side is malformed.\n */\nexport function compareVersions(left: string, right: string): number | undefined {\n  const a = parseDshVersion(left)\n  const b = parseDshVersion(right)\n  if (a === undefined || b === undefined) return undefined\n  for (const key of ['major', 'minor', 'patch'] as const) {\n    if (a[key] !== b[key]) return a[key] < b[key] ? -1 : 1\n  }\n  return comparePrerelease(a.prerelease, b.prerelease)\n}\n\n/**\n * Semver prerelease ordering: numeric identifiers compare numerically,\n * numeric identifiers rank below alphanumeric ones, alphanumeric identifiers\n * compare lexically, and a longer list wins when the shared prefix is equal.\n */\nfunction comparePrerelease(left: readonly (number | string)[], right: readonly (number | string)[]): number {\n  if (left.length === 0 && right.length === 0) return 0\n  if (left.length === 0) return 1\n  if (right.length === 0) return -1\n  const length = Math.max(left.length, right.length)\n  for (let index = 0; index < length; index += 1) {\n    const a = left[index]\n    const b = right[index]\n    if (a === undefined) return -1\n    if (b === undefined) return 1\n    if (typeof a === 'number' && typeof b === 'number') {\n      if (a !== b) return a < b ? -1 : 1\n    } else if (typeof a === 'number') {\n      return -1\n    } else if (typeof b === 'number') {\n      return 1\n    } else if (a !== b) {\n      return a < b ? -1 : 1\n    }\n  }\n  return 0\n}\n\nconst MINIMUM_RANGE_PATTERN = /^>=\\s*(v?\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+(?:-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?)$/\n\n/**\n * The bare minimum version for display: strips the `>=` operator (and an\n * optional leading `v`) from a declared requirement so UI copy that already\n * contains the comparison operator renders `0.1.1-rc.1` instead of\n * `>= >=0.1.1-rc.1`.       "content": "/**\n * The DSH runtime compatibility verdict for one declared plugin requirement,\n * evaluated the way the official boot gate evaluates it\n * (`evaluatePluginCompatibility` in app-boot's `plugin-compatibility.ts`):\n * the requirement is a node-semver range and the host satisfies it when\n * `semver.satisfies(host, range, { includePrerelease: true })` holds. Every\n * legal range form therefore decides: `||` alternatives, `^` and `~`,\n * whitespace-separated comparators, x-ranges, and prerelease tags compared as\n * ordinary versions.\n *\n * The requirement itself comes from `dshRequirementOf` in\n * `../core/version.ts`, which owns the field priority (this module only\n * decides the verdict). Host-only on purpose: `semver` is a node package and\n * must never be reachable from the browser half, which renders the same\n * declaration through the regex-only `displayMinimumVersion`.\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager/host\n */\n\nimport semver from 'semver'\n\n/**\n * The verdict for one declared requirement, with its cause kept apart so\n * callers can tell \"this host is too old\" from \"we could not check\".\n *\n * The distinction is user-visible: a `host-too-low` verdict is the only one\n * that may tell the user to upgrade DSH, because it is the only one where a\n * running version was actually compared and lost. An `unverifiable` verdict\n * means the question was never answered — an absent declaration, a range\n * node-semver rejects, or a host string that is not one valid version — so\n * telling the user to upgrade would send them after a fix nobody confirmed was\n * needed (issue #1819), and reporting it as \"below the minimum\" contradicts a\n * declaration that may well be satisfied (issue #1899).\n */\nexport type DshCompatibility =\n  | { verdict: 'satisfied' }\n  | { verdict: 'host-too-low' }\n  | { verdict: 'unverifiable' }\n\n/**\n * Decide whether the running DSH host satisfies a declared requirement range.\n * @param host - the running DSH host version.\n * @param range - the declared requirement, in any node-semver range form.\n * @returns `satisfied` when the host satisfies the declaration,\n * `host-too-low` when it was compared and does not, and `unverifiable` when\n * no comparison could be made.       "content": "/**\n * The CLI gateway: installs and removals executed by spawning the official\n * `dsh plugin --profile <name> add|remove` CLI — the single writer for the\n * profile — with a bounded job table the HTTP layer polls. In-progress jobs are never evicted. */\nconst MAX_FINISHED_JOBS = 100\n\n/**\n * Shell command-chaining metacharacters that must never reach a spawned CLI\n * argument. The gateway spawns shell-free, but the official CLI forwards to\n * pnpm with a cmd.exe shell on Windows, so a spec carrying these can still be\n * re-parsed one layer down (a failed install reported as success, or worse).\n */\nconst UNSAFE_SPEC_CHARS = /[&|<>\"'`%!\\n\\r\\0]/\n\n/**\n * Validate an install spec or package id against shell metacharacters.\n * @param spec - the user-supplied spec or id.\n * @returns the rejection message, or undefined when the spec is safe.\n */\nexport function unsafeSpecReason(spec: string): string | undefined {\n  return UNSAFE_SPEC_CHARS.test(spec)\n    ? 'plugin-manager: spec 含有危险的 shell 元字符或控制字符，已拒绝'\n    : undefined\n}\n\n/** One CLI-backed operation in flight or settled. */\nexport interface GatewayJob {\n  id: string\n  action: 'install' | 'update' | 'migrate' | 'remove'\n  spec: string\n  /** Installed package ID for an in-place npm update. */\n  targetId?: string\n  /** Exact registry version the update must land on. */\n  targetVersion?: string\n  /** Legacy package being migrated away from. */\n  sourceId?: string\n  /** Exact install spec for the target package. */\n  targetSpec?: string\n  phase: 'running' | 'done' | 'error'\n  /** The installed row on success (install) or the removed row (remove). */\n  plugin?: InstalledPluginItem\n  /** Layer changes the CLI applied, normalized for the conflict panel. */\n  conflicts?: ControlChange[]\n  /**\n   * Duplicate-mount safeguard notices: bundles entries the CLI's\n   * reconciliation added but the composition already mounted through a patch\n   * row, stripped back out so the next boot cannot double-mount. Each notice\n   * carries the conflict-row shape (the entry left the bundles layer:\n   * enabled -> uninstalled) so the tab can render it with the existing rows;\n   * the package itself stays installed and row-mounted.\n   */\n  notices?: ControlChange[]\n  /**\n   * Bundles whose new version is on disk but not loaded in this process: the\n   * official manager answered `application: 'restart-required'` for the run\n   * that applied it, so the plugin is installed and its rows are gone until the\n   * host restarts (issue #1905). depth < 12; depth += 1) {\n      const parent = pathApi.dirname(current)\n      if (parent === current) break\n      current = parent\n      // macOS spells the directory `Resources`; the match is case-insensitive\n      // because a false positive only ever yields a candidate that must exist.\n      if (pathApi.basename(current).toLowerCase() === 'resources') {\n        roots.push(current)\n        break\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  return roots\n}\n\n/**\n * Electron's resource directory when this process is an Electron child, read\n * defensively: the type is not in `@types/node`, and a plain Node host has no\n * such property at all.\n */\nfunction processResourcesPath(): string | undefined {\n  const value = (process as unknown as { resourcesPath?: unknown }).resourcesPath\n  return typeof value === 'string' && value !== '' ? value : undefined\n}\n\n/** The binary search roots for the dsh CLI. */\nexport function findDshBinary(\n  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env,\n  platform: string = process.platform,\n  exists: (path: string) => boolean = existsSync,\n  hostEntryPath: string | undefined = process.argv[1],\n  resourcesPath: string | undefined = processResourcesPath(),\n): string | null {\n  const candidates: string[] = []\n  const separator = platform === 'win32' ? ';' : ':'\n  const pathApi = platform === 'win32' ? win32 : posix\n  for (const dir of (env.PATH ?? '').split(separator)) {\n    if (dir === '') continue\n    if (platform === 'win32') {\n      candidates.push(`${dir}\\\\dsh.cmd`, `${dir}\\\\dsh.exe`)\n    } else {\n      candidates.push(`${dir}/dsh`)\n    }\n  }\n  // A local wrapper or npx launch may omit its node_modules/.bin directory\n  // from PATH. Walk up from the actual host entry script and probe each npm\n  // project root without guessing from the DSH_HOME profile location.\n  if (hostEntryPath !== undefined && hostEntryPath !== '') {\n    let current = pathApi.dirname(hostEntryPath)\n    for (let depth = 0; depth < 10; depth += 1) {\n      const binDir = pathApi.join(current, 'node_modules', '.bin')\n      if (platform === 'win32') candidates.push(pathApi.join(binDir, 'dsh.cmd'), pathApi.join(binDir, 'dsh.exe'))\n      else candidates.push(pathApi.join(binDir, 'dsh'))\n      const parent = pathApi.dirname(current)\n      if (parent === current) break\n      current = parent\n    }\n  }\n  if (platform === 'darwin') {\n    candidates.push('/opt/homebrew/bin/dsh', '/usr/local/bin/dsh')\n  }\n  // Packages and the desktop app put the CLI in reach of their own files, not\n  // on PATH, so also probe the siblings of the running host's entry script:\n  //   <runtime>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/bin.js\n  //   <runtime>/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib/../../.bin/dsh.cmd\n  // The npm-published desktop runtime strips every node_modules/.bin directory\n  // (symlinked shims cannot survive an installer), so the package's own lib/bin.js\n  // is the only launchable form there (issue #1588).\n  if (hostEntryPath !== undefined && hostEntryPath !== '') {\n    const entryDir = pathApi.dirname(hostEntryPath)\n    const packageRoot = pathApi.dirname(entryDir)\n    candidates.push(pathApi.join(packageRoot, 'lib', 'bin.js'))\n  }\n  // The packaged Desktop installer puts the CLI nowhere near the running host:\n  // the private host package ships only lib/index.js and lib/cli.js (no\n  // lib/bin.js), every node_modules/.bin directory is stripped, and the CLI\n  // launcher lives in a sibling resource tree\n  // (<resources>/runtime/cli/bin/dsh.cmd on Windows, .../dsh elsewhere) that\n  // the launcher never adds to the host's PATH — it prepends only\n  // <resources>/runtime/bin, which carries node alone. Without this candidate\n  // the packaged Desktop has no CLI at all, and every version probe and\n  // CLI-backed write fails closed (#1819, following #1588).\n  for (const root of desktopResourceRoots(hostEntryPath, resourcesPath, pathApi)) {\n    const cliBin = pathApi.join(root, 'runtime', 'cli', 'bin')\n    if (platform === 'win32') {\n      candidates.push(pathApi.join(cliBin, 'dsh.cmd'), pathApi.join(cliBin, 'dsh.exe'))\n    } else {\n      candidates.push(pathApi.join(cliBin, 'dsh'))\n    }\n  }\n  for (const candidate of candidates) {\n    if (exists(candidate)) return candidate\n  }\n  return null\n}\n\n/**\n * Append bounded CLI output (stdout + stderr interleaved is not preserved;\n * tail wins). Bytes are accumulated and decoded once at read time: a Windows\n * console writes its OEM code page (CP936/GBK on zh-CN), so per-chunk\n * `toString()` both mis-decodes the encoding and splits characters that\n * straddle two reads into replacement characters (issue #1600).\n */\nfunction capture(chunk: Buffer, buffer: OutputCapture): void {\n  buffer.push(chunk)\n}\n\n/** Bytes read for the shebang probe (a Node script names its interpreter on line 1). */\nconst SHEBANG_PROBE_BYTES = 256\n\n/**\n * Read a file's leading bytes for the shebang probe. Every failure — a missing\n * file, a directory, a permission error, an unreadable asar entry — reads as\n * \"no head\", so the caller falls back to spawning the path directly.\n * @param path - file to probe.\n * @returns the leading text, or undefined.\n */\nexport function readFileHead(path: string): string | undefined {\n  let fd: number | undefined\n  try {\n    fd = openSync(path, 'r')\n    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(SHEBANG_PROBE_BYTES)\n    const read = readSync(fd, buffer, 0, SHEBANG_PROBE_BYTES, 0)\n    return buffer.subarray(0, read).toString('utf8')\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  } finally {\n    if (fd !== undefined) {\n      try {\n        closeSync(fd)\n      } catch {\n        // Already closed or never opened: nothing to release.\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether a resolved CLI path is a Node script: a `.js` module, or a file whose\n * shebang names node. A Node script cannot be spawned as an executable on its\n * own: the kernel hands the shebang to the interpreter it names, and\n * `#!/usr/bin/env node` resolves node through PATH — which a GUI-launched host\n * (the packaged Desktop app) does not carry, so the child dies before the CLI\n * starts with `env: node: No such file or directory` (exit 127).\n * @param path - the resolved CLI path.\n * @param readHead - head probe (test seam).\n * @returns true when the path needs a Node interpreter.\n */\nexport function isNodeScript(path: string, readHead: (path: string) => string | undefined = readFileHead): boolean {\n  if (/\\.(?:c|m)?js$/i.test(path)) return true\n  const head = readHead(path)\n  if (head === undefined) return false\n  const firstLine = head.split('\\n', 1)[0] ?? ''\n  return /^#!.*\\bnode\\b/.test(firstLine)\n}\n\n/**\n * The spawn command for the dsh CLI on this platform. A Node script (the\n * npm/homebrew `dsh` shim, a `.bin` symlink, a packaged `lib/bin.js`) is run\n * by an interpreter that exists regardless of PATH: a `node` sitting beside the\n * CLI when the installation ships one (npm-global and homebrew layouts), else\n * the host's own interpreter — `process.execPath`, which the ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE\n * branch in {@link spawnDsh} covers for an Electron host. Either header is stamped by a\n * hop that forwards traffic, so the request did not originate on this machine.\n * @param request - node HTTP request.\n * @returns true when a forwarding header is present.\n */\nexport function isProxiedRequest(request: IncomingMessage): boolean {\n  return request.headers['cf-connecting-ip'] !== undefined\n    || request.headers['x-forwarded-for'] !== undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * Request-level trust fence: a loopback socket address AND a loopback Host\n * header, plus browser same-origin markers.       "content": "/**\n * Profile resolution and manifest reads for the gateway host half. The npm\n * web runtime has no plugin-installer service, so this package resolves the\n * boot profile from the host process's own argv (the launcher fact) and reads\n * the profile's package.json and cordis.patch.yml directly — reads only; every\n * write goes through the official CLI or the patch-row editor.\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager/host\n */\n\nimport { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'\nimport { copyFile, readFile, rename, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'\nimport { basename, dirname, isAbsolute, join, normalize, sep } from 'node:path'\nimport { resolveDshHome } from './dsh-home.ts'\n\n/**\n * The launched-profile slice the official runtime publishes on the host\n * context as `profileContext` (`{ name, dir, patchPath, installAnchor, ... }`).\n * It is a contract observation, not an import: the gateway needs the same\n * three facts the runtime already resolved, and rebuilding them from\n * `--profile` / `DSH_HOME` cannot name the profile on a launcher that passes\n * neither. Its `version` IS the version\n   * of the DSH this process booted, so it answers the compatibility question\n   * without spawning anything; on a packaged Desktop install it is the only\n   * source that does, because no `dsh` reaches that host's PATH (issue #1819).\n   */\n  installAnchor?: unknown\n}\n\n/** Resolved locations of one profile's writable surface. */\nexport interface ProfileFacts {\n  /** Profile name (the directory under $DSH_HOME/profiles). */\n  profileName: string\n  /** Absolute profile directory. */\n  profileDir: string\n  /** Absolute path of the profile's cordis.patch.yml. */\n  patchPath: string\n  /** Absolute path of the profile's package.json. */\n  packageJsonPath: string\n  /** True when the profile was inferred from the packaged desktop host. */\n  desktop?: boolean\n}\n\n/**\n * Strip a leading UTF-8 byte order mark (U+FEFF), which commonly appears in\n * files edited or created on Windows (PowerShell / Notepad).\n */\nexport function stripBom(text: string): string {\n  return text.charCodeAt(0) === 0xFEFF ? text.slice(1) : text\n}\n\n/** Read the packaged desktop app's persisted active profile, when present. */\nexport function desktopSelectedProfile(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): string | undefined {\n  const explicit = env.DSH_DESKTOP_DEFAULT_PROFILE?.trim()\n  if (explicit) return explicit\n  const appRoots = [\n    env.APPDATA && join(env.APPDATA, 'DSH Desktop'),\n    env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME && join(env.XDG_CONFIG_HOME, 'DSH Desktop'),\n    env.HOME && join(env.HOME, 'Library', 'Application Support', 'DSH Desktop'),\n    env.HOME && join(env.HOME, '.config', 'DSH Desktop'),\n  ].filter((value): value is string => typeof value === 'string')\n  for (const root of appRoots) {\n    try {\n      const parsed = JSON.parse(stripBom(readFileSync(join(root, 'profile-selection', 'state.json'), 'utf8'))) as { active?: unknown }\n      if (typeof parsed.active === 'string' && parsed.active.trim() !== '') return parsed.active.trim()\n    } catch {\n      // Missing or malformed desktop state: try the next platform location.\n    }\n  }\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * The running installation's own `@deepseek-ai/dsh` package.json, as the\n * launcher published it on `profileContext`, or undefined when the host\n * publishes none (or publishes something unusable). This is a READ-ONLY\n * fact — unlike the profile directory and the patch path it is never a write\n * target — but it still arrives from outside this package, so it must be an\n * absolute, traversal-free path before anything reads a version out of it.\n * @param launched - the profile facts the Host published, when available.\n * @returns the validated anchor path, or undefined.\n */\nexport function launchedInstallAnchor(launched: LaunchedProfile | undefined): string | undefined {\n  const anchor = launched === undefined || typeof launched.installAnchor !== 'string'\n    ? ''\n    : launched.installAnchor.trim()\n  if (anchor === '') return undefined\n  if (!isAbsolute(anchor) || anchor.split(/[\\/\\\\]/).includes('..')) return undefined\n  return anchor\n}\n\n/**\n * Read the `version` field of one package manifest, tolerating every failure:\n * a missing file, an unreadable one (a stripped asar entry), malformed JSON, or\n * a non-string version all read as \"no version\". Callers fall back to their next\n * source rather than reporting a version nobody declared.\n * @param manifestPath - absolute path of a package.json.\n * @returns the declared version, or undefined.\n */\nexport function readManifestVersion(manifestPath: string): string | undefined {\n  try {\n    const parsed = JSON.parse(stripBom(readFileSync(manifestPath, 'utf8'))) as { version?: unknown }\n    return typeof parsed.version === 'string' && parsed.version.trim() !== '' ? parsed.version.trim() : undefined\n  } catch {\n    return undefined\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether the host argv names the packaged Desktop launcher, whose entry\n * script is `@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-host`. The Desktop client boots the\n * `desktop` profile through `runProfile()` WITHOUT a `--profile` flag and\n * without exporting DSH_PROFILE, so argv is the only launcher fact left and\n * the desktop channel probe must stay on for that shape (the packaged host\n * registers the official installer services programmatically, which the CLI\n * boot dump cannot see).\n * @param argv - process argv.\n */\nexport function isPackagedDesktopArgv(argv: readonly string[]): boolean {\n  return argv.some(argument => argument.includes(`${sep}dsh-desktop-host${sep}`) || argument.includes('/dsh-desktop-host/'))\n}\n\n/**\n * The profile directory a packaged Desktop launch carries in its OWN argv.\n * Electron under ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE (and node alike) strips exec switches\n * from `process.argv`, so the desktop host launches as\n * `[execPath, dsh-desktop-host/lib/index.js, <dsh>, <profileDir>, ...]` and\n * hands the profile directory to its own `loadProfileDirectory` as that\n * positional argument. This is a launcher fact independent of the\n * `profileContext` service, so a runtime that publishes no service can\n * still be named correctly; a published service stays authoritative above it.\n * @param argv - process argv.\n * @returns the absolute profile directory, or undefined when argv names none.\n */\nexport function desktopProfileDirFromArgv(argv: readonly string[]): string | undefined {\n  if (!isPackagedDesktopArgv(argv)) return undefined\n  for (const argument of argv) {\n    // The profile directory is the one absolute argument inside a\n    // `profiles` tree; the launcher entry, the dsh install and the\n    // runtime roots all sit elsewhere, so no positional index is assumed.\n    if (!isAbsolute(argument)) continue\n    if (basename(dirname(argument)) !== 'profiles') continue\n    const name = basename(argument)\n    if (name === '' || name === '.' || name === '..') continue\n    return argument\n  }\n  return undefined\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve the boot profile from the launcher facts: an explicit `--profile`\n * flag wins, then the profile the official runtime published on the host\n * context, then the profile directory a packaged launch carries in its own\n * argv, then the DSH_PROFILE environment override, then the `web` subcommand\n * alias, then the packaged Desktop app's persisted selection.\n *\n * Why the launched facts outrank DSH_PROFILE: in this runtime the variable is\n * an OUTPUT, not a boot selector. `runProfile()` is the single launch path for\n * CLI and Desktop alike and provides `profileContext` in both, and\n * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-shell-env` DERIVES `DSH_PROFILE` from `profileContext.name`\n * for the shell children it spawns; no runtime module reads it to choose a\n * profile. Whenever both exist they therefore describe the same profile, and\n * the service carries the more precise facts (the exact directory and patch\n * file). A hand-set or stale value disagreeing with the running host is the\n * one case where the order matters, and following it would mount the gateway -\n * and write its rows - into a profile this host never reads.\n * @param argv - process argv (test seam).\n * @param env - process environment (test seam).\n * @param launched - the profile facts the Host published, when available.\n * @param desktopLauncher - whether argv names the packaged Desktop launcher.\n * @returns the resolved profile facts.\n */\nexport function resolveProfile(\n  argv: readonly string[] = process.argv,\n  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env,\n  launched?: LaunchedProfile,\n  desktopLauncher: boolean = isPackagedDesktopArgv(argv),\n): ProfileFacts {\n  const flagIndex = argv.indexOf('--profile')\n  if (flagIndex !== -1 && argv[flagIndex + 1] !== undefined && argv[flagIndex + 1] !== '') {\n    return factsFor(argv[flagIndex + 1], env, desktopLauncher)\n  }\n  // The published profile outranks the environment: a Desktop workaround may\n  // set DSH_PROFILE globally while the running host boots another profile, and\n  // following the variable there would mount the gateway (and write patch\n  // rows) into a profile this host never reads. The service is the runtime's\n  // own answer about the profile it actually launched.\n  const published = launchedFacts(launched, desktopLauncher, env)\n  if (published !== undefined) return published\n  // No service (an older runtime): the packaged Desktop launcher still names\n  // its profile directory positionally in argv, which outranks the\n  // environment for the same reason the published service does.\n  const desktopDir = desktopProfileDirFromArgv(argv)\n  if (desktopDir !== undefined) {\n    // Built through the same validated path as a published directory so the\n    // argv fact cannot skip a guard the service fact must pass.\n    const argvFacts = launchedFacts({ name: basename(desktopDir), dir: desktopDir }, desktopLauncher, env)\n    if (argvFacts !== undefined) return argvFacts\n  }\n  if (env.DSH_PROFILE !== undefined && env.DSH_PROFILE.trim() !== '') {\n    // A Desktop workaround may set DSH_PROFILE globally. Its in-process boot\n    // still has only the executable in argv; keep desktop channel probing in\n    // that shape, while ordinary CLI invocations remain non-desktop.\n    const name = env.DSH_PROFILE.trim()\n    const desktop = desktopLauncher || (argv.length <= 1 && desktopSelectedProfile(env) === name)\n    return factsFor(name, env, desktop)\n  }\n  if (argv.includes('web')) return factsFor('web', env, desktopLauncher)\n  const selected = desktopSelectedProfile(env)\n  if (selected !== undefined) return factsFor(selected, env, true)\n  throw new Error('plugin-manager: cannot determine the boot profile; pass --profile <name> or set DSH_PROFILE')\n}\n\n/**\n * Facts from the profile the Host published on `profileContext`, when that\n * service carries a usable name (or directory). The published directory is the\n * launched profile's real location, which is exactly what the runtime passes\n * to the profile loader itself — the name-based builder would only reproduce\n * it. It is still validated before it becomes the root of every later lookup.\n * @param launched - the host's published profile facts.\n * @param desktopLauncher - whether argv names the packaged Desktop launcher.\n * @param env - process environment, for the name-only fallback layout.\n * @returns the facts, or undefined when nothing usable was published.\n */\nfunction launchedFacts(\n  launched: LaunchedProfile | undefined,\n  desktopLauncher: boolean,\n  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv,\n): ProfileFacts | undefined {\n  if (launched === undefined) return undefined\n  const name = typeof launched.name === 'string' ? launched.name.trim() : ''\n  const dir = typeof launched.dir === 'string' ? launched.dir.trim() : ''\n  if (name === '' && dir === '') return undefined\n  if (name !== '') assertSafeProfileName(name)\n  const profileRoot = join(resolveDshHome(env), 'profiles')\n  const profileDir = dir !== '' ? dir : join(profileRoot, name)\n  // The published directory becomes the root of every later lookup (module\n  // manifests, row patches, the --dump-config probe) and the place row writes\n  // land, so its SHAPE is validated here. The RAW segments are inspected\n  // because `normalize` would silently collapse a `..` away, hiding an escape\n  // instead of rejecting it.\n  if (!isAbsolute(profileDir) || profileDir.split(/[\\/\\\\]/).includes('..')) {\n    throw new Error(`plugin-manager: published profile directory is not a safe absolute path ${JSON.stringify(launched.dir ?? '')}`)\n  }\n  // The published name and directory must describe the SAME profile: the name\n  // drives every CLI `--profile <name>` spawn while the directory drives the\n  // files this gateway reads and writes, so a mismatch would split the two\n  // write paths across different profiles. The official runtime publishes\n  // exactly `basename(dir)` as the name, so this holds for every real host.\n  const dirBase = profileDir.split(/[\\/\\\\]/).filter(Boolean).pop() ?? basename(profileDir)\n  if (name !== '' && name !== dirBase) {\n    throw new Error(`plugin-manager: published profile name and directory disagree ${JSON.stringify(name)} vs ${JSON.stringify(profileDir)}`)\n  }\n  const isPosixLiteral = profileDir.includes('/') && !profileDir.includes('\\\\')\n  const ownPatchPath = isPosixLiteral ? `${profileDir}/cordis.patch.yml` : join(profileDir, 'cordis.patch.yml')\n  const publishedPatchPath = typeof launched.patchPath === 'string' ? launched.patchPath.trim() : ''\n  // The patch path is a WRITE target (row enablement). Accept only the\n  // profile's own patch file; anything else would let the published value\n  // redirect a write outside the profile this gateway mounts.\n  if (publishedPatchPath !== '' && publishedPatchPath !== ownPatchPath && normalize(publishedPatchPath) !== normalize(ownPatchPath)) {\n    throw new Error(`plugin-manager: published patch path is not the launched profile's own patch file ${JSON.stringify(launched.patchPath)}`)\n  }\n  return {\n    profileName: name !== '' ? name : dirBase,\n    profileDir,\n    patchPath: ownPatchPath,\n    packageJsonPath: isPosixLiteral ? `${profileDir}/package.json` : join(profileDir, 'package.json'),\n    // Strictly a launcher fact: only argv naming the packaged Desktop host (or\n    // the persisted desktop selection, in the fallback branch below) marks the\n    // run as desktop. A profile that merely happens to be *named* \"desktop\" is\n    // not evidence about the host, and /mode's installer-service probe keys on\n    // the real host shape.\n    desktop: desktopLauncher,\n  }\n}\n\n/** Facts for one explicitly named profile, resolved under `$DSH_HOME/profiles`. */\nfunction factsFor(name: string, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, desktop: boolean): ProfileFacts {\n  const trimmed = name.trim()\n  assertSafeProfileName(trimmed)\n  const profileDir = join(resolveDshHome(env), 'profiles', trimmed)\n  return {\n    profileName: trimmed,\n    profileDir,\n    patchPath: join(profileDir, 'cordis.patch.yml'),\n    packageJsonPath: join(profileDir, 'package.json'),\n    desktop,\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Reject a profile name that is not exactly one directory segment under\n * `profiles/`. `.` is rejected alongside separators and `..`: `join` normalizes\n * it away, so accepting it would silently resolve to the `profiles` directory\n * itself rather than to a profile.\n */\nfunction assertSafeProfileName(name: string): void {\n  if (name === '' || name === '.' || name === '..' || name.includes('/') || name.includes('\\\\')) {\n    throw new Error(`plugin-manager: invalid profile name ${JSON.stringify(name)}`)\n  }\n}\n\n/** The profile package.json surface the gateway reads. */\nexport interface ProfileManifest {\n  /** dsh.profile.bundles entries (may be absent). */\n  bundles: string[]\n  /** package.json dependencies: package name -> install spec. */\n  dependencies: Record<string, string>\n}\n\n/**\n * Read the profile manifest; half mirrors. */\nexport const GATEWAY_PREFIX = '/api/plugin-manager'\n\n/** Registry timeout for one update check. */\nconst REGISTRY_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000\n\n/** Deadline for one dsh --version probe.       "content": "/**\n * Host half of the dsh-plugin-manager plugin — runs in the DSH host process.\n *\n * Dual-channel design: on runtimes with the official installer services\n * (DSHCode and the 1.0.4 checkout web), the browser half uses the official\n * `/plugin-installer` and `/plugin-control` RPC channels and this half does\n * nothing. It must not repeat an id another bundle already claims: the\n * loader keeps one entry per id, so a shared id would also give two host\n * halves one cordis plugin name.\n */\nexport const name = 'ui-plugin-manager-update-check'\n\n/** Services the gateway needs — the web server seam. */\nexport const inject = ['webServer']\n\n/** Apply the host half (once per process). */\nexport const apply = mountOnce('@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-plugin-manager', applyImpl)\n\n/**\n * The launched profile the official runtime publishes on the host context\n * (`profileContext`, `{ name, dir, patchPath, ... }`). The packaged Desktop\n * launcher boots \"desktop\" through `runProfile()` with neither a `--profile`\n * flag nor a DSH_PROFILE variable, so this service is the only launcher fact\n * that names the running profile there; a CLI-booted host keeps resolving from\n * argv and the environment exactly as before. It is an OPTIONAL read, not an\n * injected dependency: hosts without the service simply fall through.\n * @param ctx - host plugin context.\n * @returns the published facts, or undefined when the host publishes none.\n */\nfunction launchedProfile(ctx: Context): LaunchedProfile | undefined {\n  const facts = ctx.get('profileContext') as LaunchedProfile | undefined\n  return facts === undefined || facts === null ? undefined : facts\n}\n\n/**\n * The official in-process plugin manager, when the running host mounts one.\n * `@deepseek-ai/dsh-plugin-manager` registers itself as the `pluginManager`\n * service (a TypertRemoteService, which is an ordinary Cordis Service under\n * that key); this is the same writer the official Plugins page drives, read here\n * as a contract observation rather than an import — the repository builds\n * against the official SDK's public packages, and this package must keep\n * running when a host mounts no manager at all. Only an application-owned\n * profile uses it (see CliGateway), because there the CLI refuses the profile.\n * @param ctx - host plugin context.\n * @returns the manager, or undefined when the host publishes none.\n */\nfunction officialManager(ctx: Context): NativePluginManager | undefined {\n  // Called as a method on the context: the service lookup reads the context's\n  // own registry, so the receiver must stay intact.\n  const manager = (ctx as unknown as { get(name: string): unknown }).get('pluginManager')\n  return manager === undefined || manager === null ? undefined : manager as NativePluginManager\n}\n\nfunction applyImpl(ctx: Context): void {\n  // Gateway mode needs the boot profile; the launched profile the Host\n  // publishes is authoritative when the launcher passed no flag and no\n  // environment override (the packaged Desktop client). The anchor is read\n  // from the same published profile facts the profile resolution already used.\n  const installAnchor = launchedInstallAnchor(launched)\n\n  ctx.effect(() => {\n    const disposers = makeGatewayRoutes({ facts, gateway, cliAvailable, installAnchor })\n      .map(route => ctx.webServer.register(route))\n    return () => {\n      for (const dispose of disposers) dispose()\n    }\n  }, 'plugin-manager: gateway routes')\n\n  // A bundle that renamed a row's package leaves every profile row that named\n  // the old one dead (issue #1901 moved the aggregate's family rows from the\n  // `@linxin666/dsh-web-all/<family>` subpath to the real package, and the\n  // loader skips a row whose name does not match the inserted row).
